                                           RISKS IN RELATION TO THE FIRST OFFER
This being the first public offer of the Equity Shares of our Company, there has been no formal market for the Equity Shares. The face
value of the Equity Shares is ₹10 each. The Floor Price, Cap Price and Offer Price as determined by our Company, in consultation with
the Book Running Lead Managers (“BRLMs”), and on the basis of assessment of market demand for the Equity Shares by way of the
Book Building Process, in accordance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations and as stated in “Basis for Offer Price” beginning on page 124
should not be considered to be indicative of the market price of the Equity Shares after the Equity Shares are listed. No assurance can be
given regarding an active and/or sustained trading in the Equity Shares nor regarding the price at which the Equity Shares will be traded
after listing.

                                                              GENERAL RISK
Investments in equity and equity-related securities involve a degree of risk and Bidders should not invest any funds in the Offer unless
they can afford to take the risk of losing their entire investment. Bidders are advised to read the risk factors carefully before taking an
investment decision in the Offer. For taking an investment decision, Bidders must rely on their own examination of our Company and the
Offer, including the risks involved. The Equity Shares in the Offer have neither been recommended, nor approved by the Securities and
Exchange Board of India (“SEBI”), nor does SEBI guarantee the accuracy or adequacy of the contents of this Updated Draft Red Herring
Prospectus – I. Specific attention of the investors is invited to “Risk Factors” on page 20.

   Our Company was originally incorporated as ‘Paramotor Digital Technology Private Limited’, as a private limited company under the Companies Act, 2013, pursuant to a certificate of incorporation dated November 4, 2016, issued by the
   Registrar of Companies, Central Registration Centre. Subsequently, our Company was converted from a private limited company into a public limited company pursuant to a board resolution dated January 21, 2026 and a special resolution
   passed by our Shareholders in an extra-ordinary general meeting on January 21, 2026 and consequently the name of our Company was changed to ‘Paramotor Digital Technology Limited’, and a fresh certificate of incorporation dated
   January 30, 2026 was issued by the Registrar of Companies, Central Processing Centre. For details in relation to changes in the registered office of our Company, see “History and Certain Corporate Matters – Changes in the Registered
   Office” on page 244.

INITIAL PUBLIC OFFER OF [●] EQUITY SHARES OF FACE VALUE OF ₹10 EACH (“EQUITY SHARES”) OF PARAMOTOR DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY LIMITED (“COMPANY”) FOR CASH AT A PRICE OF ₹[●] PER EQUITY SHARE
(INCLUDING A SHARE PREMIUM OF ₹[●] PER EQUITY SHARE) (“OFFER PRICE”) AGGREGATING UP TO ₹10,000.00 MILLION (THE “OFFER”) COMPRISING A FRESH ISSUE OF [●] EQUITY SHARES OF FACE VALUE OF ₹10 EACH
AGGREGATING UP TO ₹6,980.00 MILLION BY OUR COMPANY (“FRESH ISSUE”) AND AN OFFER FOR SALE OF [●] EQUITY SHARES OF FACE VALUE OF ₹10 EACH AGGREGATING UP TO ₹3,020.00 MILLION (THE “OFFER FOR
SALE”), CONSISTING OF [●] EQUITY SHARES OF FACE VALUE OF ₹10 EACH AGGREGATING UP TO ₹1,510.00 MILLION BY SONIA PANKAJ ASHER AND [●] EQUITY SHARES OF FACE VALUE OF ₹10 EACH AGGREGATING UP
TO ₹1,510.00 MILLION BY RAHUL ANAND (COLLECTIVELY, THE “PROMOTER SELLING SHAREHOLDERS”, AND SUCH EQUITY SHARES, THE “OFFERED SHARES”).

OUR COMPANY, IN CONSULTATION WITH THE BRLMS, MAY CONSIDER A PRE-IPO PLACEMENT OF SPECIFIED SECURITIES FOR AN AMOUNT AGGREGATING UP TO ₹ 1,396.00 MILLION, IN ONE OR MORE TRANCHES, AS
MAY BE PERMITTED UNDER APPLICABLE LAW, AT OUR DISCRETION, PRIOR TO FILING OF THE RED HERRING PROSPECTUS WITH THE ROC. THE PRE-IPO PLACEMENT, IF UNDERTAKEN, WILL BE AT A PRICE TO BE
DECIDED BY OUR COMPANY, IN CONSULTATION WITH THE BRLMS. IF THE PRE-IPO PLACEMENT IS COMPLETED, THE AMOUNT RAISED PURSUANT TO THE PRE-IPO PLACEMENT WILL BE REDUCED FROM THE FRESH
ISSUE, SUBJECT TO COMPLIANCE WITH RULE 19(2)(B) OF THE SECURITIES CONTRACTS (REGULATION) RULES, 1957, AS AMENDED. THE PRE-IPO PLACEMENT, IF UNDERTAKEN, SHALL NOT EXCEED 20% OF THE SIZE OF
THE FRESH ISSUE. PRIOR TO THE COMPLETION OF THE OFFER, OUR COMPANY SHALL APPROPRIATELY INTIMATE THE SUBSCRIBERS TO THE PRE-IPO PLACEMENT, PRIOR TO ALLOTMENT PURSUANT TO THE PRE-
IPO PLACEMENT, THAT THERE IS NO GUARANTEE THAT OUR COMPANY MAY PROCEED WITH THE OFFER OR THE OFFER MAY BE SUCCESSFUL AND WILL RESULT INTO LISTING OF THE EQUITY SHARES ON THE
STOCK EXCHANGES. FURTHER, RELEVANT DISCLOSURES IN RELATION TO SUCH INTIMATION TO THE SUBSCRIBERS TO THE PRE-IPO PLACEMENT (IF UNDERTAKEN) SHALL BE APPROPRIATELY MADE IN THE
RELEVANT SECTIONS OF THE RED HERRING PROSPECTUS AND THE PROSPECTUS. OUR COMPANY SHALL REPORT ANY PRE-IPO PLACEMENT TO THE STOCK EXCHANGES, WITHIN 24 HOURS OF SUCH PRE-IPO
PLACEMENT (IN PART OR IN ENTIRETY) AND AS MAY BE REQUIRED UNDER APPLICABLE LAW.

THE OFFER INCLUDES A RESERVATION OF [●] EQUITY SHARES OF FACE VALUE OF ₹10 EACH, AGGREGATING UP TO ₹[●] MILLION (CONSTITUTING UP TO [●]% OF THE POST-OFFER PAID-UP EQUITY SHARE CAPITAL),
FOR SUBSCRIPTION BY ELIGIBLE EMPLOYEES (“EMPLOYEE RESERVATION PORTION”). OUR COMPANY, IN CONSULTATION WITH THE BRLMs MAY OFFER A DISCOUNT OF UP TO [●]% OF THE OFFER PRICE TO ELIGIBLE
EMPLOYEES BIDDING IN THE EMPLOYEE RESERVATION PORTION (“EMPLOYEE DISCOUNT”), SUBJECT TO NECESSARY APPROVALS AS MAY BE REQUIRED. THE OFFER LESS THE EMPLOYEE RESERVATION PORTION
IS HEREINAFTER REFERRED TO AS THE “NET OFFER”. THE OFFER AND THE NET OFFER SHALL CONSTITUTE [●]% AND [●]% OF THE POST-OFFER PAID-UP EQUITY SHARE CAPITAL OF OUR COMPANY, RESPECTIVELY.

THE FACE VALUE OF EQUITY SHARES IS ₹10 EACH. THE OFFER PRICE IS [●] TIMES THE FACE VALUE OF THE EQUITY SHARES. THE PRICE BAND AND THE MINIMUM BID LOT WILL BE DECIDED BY OUR COMPANY, IN
CONSULTATION WITH THE BOOK RUNNING LEAD MANAGERS AND WILL BE ADVERTISED IN ALL EDITIONS OF FINANCIAL EXPRESS, AN ENGLISH NATIONAL DAILY NEWSPAPER, ALL EDITIONS OF JANSATTA, A HINDI
NATIONAL DAILY NEWSPAPER AND MUMBAI EDITION OF NAVSHAKTI, A MARATHI DAILY NEWSPAPER (MARATHI BEING THE REGIONAL LANGUAGE OF MAHARASHTRA, WHERE OUR REGISTERED OFFICE IS LOCATED)
EACH WITH WIDE CIRCULATION, AT LEAST TWO WORKING DAYS PRIOR TO THE BID/ OFFER OPENING DATE AND SHALL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO BSE AND NSE (TOGETHER WITH BSE, THE “STOCK EXCHANGES”) FOR
THE PURPOSE OF UPLOADING ON THEIR RESPECTIVE WEBSITES IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE SEBI ICDR REGULATIONS.
In case of any revision in the Price Band, the Bid/ Offer Period will be extended by at least three additional Working Days after such revision in the Price Band, subject to the Bid/ Offer Period not exceeding 10 Working Days. In cases of force majeure, banking strike or
similar unforeseen circumstances, our Company in consultation with the BRLMs, may for reasons to be recorded in writing, extend the Bid/ Offer Period for a minimum of one Working Day, subject to the Bid/ Offer Period not exceeding 10 Working Days. Any revision
in the Price Band and the revised Bid/ Offer Period, if applicable, shall be widely disseminated by notification to the Stock Exchanges, by issuing a public notice, and also by indicating the change on the respective websites of the BRLMs and at the terminals of the
Syndicate Members and by intimation to Self-Certified Syndicate Banks (“SCSBs”), the Designated Intermediaries and the Sponsor Banks, as applicable.
The Offer is being made in terms of Rule 19(2)(b) of the SCRR read with Regulation 31 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations. The Offer is being made through the Book Building Process (as defined hereinafter) in accordance with Regulation 6(2) of the SEBI ICDR Regulations
wherein in terms of Regulation 32(2) of the SEBI ICDR Regulations, not less than 75% of the Net Offer shall be available for allocation on a proportionate basis to QIBs (and such portion, the “QIB Portion”) provided that our Company in consultation with the BRLMs,
may allocate up to 60% of the QIB Portion to Anchor Investors on a discretionary basis in accordance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations (“Anchor Investor Portion”), of which, 40% of the Anchor Investor Portion shall be reserved in the following manner: (a) 33.33%
shall be reserved for domestic Mutual Funds; and (b) 6.67% shall be reserved for Life Insurance Companies and Pension Funds, subject to valid Bids being received from domestic Mutual Funds, Life Insurance Companies and Pension Funds at or above the Anchor
Investor Allocation Price. In the event of under-subscription or non-allocation in the Anchor Investor Portion, the balance Equity Shares shall be added to the QIB Portion (excluding the Anchor Investor Portion) (“Net QIB Portion”). Further, 5% of the Net QIB Portion
shall be available for allocation on a proportionate basis only to Mutual Funds and the remainder of the Net QIB Portion shall be available for allocation on a proportionate basis to all QIB Bidders (other than Anchor Investors) including Mutual Funds, subject to valid
Bids being received at or above the Offer Price. However, if the aggregate demand from Mutual Funds is less than 5% of the Net QIB Portion, the balance Equity Shares available for allocation in the Mutual Fund Portion will be added to the remaining QIB Portion for
proportionate allocation to QIBs. Further, not more than 15% of the Net Offer shall be available for allocation to Non-Institutional Bidders out of which (a) one-third of such portion shall be reserved for applicants with application size of more than ₹0.20 million and up
to ₹1.00 million; and (b) two-third of such portion shall be reserved for applicants with application size of more than ₹1.00 million provided that the unsubscribed portion in either of such sub-categories may be allocated to applicants in the other sub-category of Non-
Institutional Bidders and not more than 10% of the Net Offer shall be available for allocation to RIBs in accordance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations, subject to valid Bids being received from them at or above the Offer Price. Further, Equity Shares will be allocated on
a proportionate basis to Eligible Employees applying under the Employee Reservation Portion, subject to valid Bids being received from them at or above the Offer Price (net of Employee Discount, if any, as applicable. All potential Bidders (except Anchor Investors)
are required to mandatorily utilise the Application Supported by Blocked Amount (“ASBA”) process by providing details of their respective bank accounts (including UPI ID for UPI Bidders) (as defined hereinafter) in which the Bid Amount will be blocked by the
SCSBs or the Sponsor Bank(s), as applicable, to participate in the Offer. Anchor Investors are not permitted to participate in the Anchor Investor Portion of the Offer through the ASBA process. See “Offer Procedure” on page 395.

                                           DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS

This Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus – I uses certain definitions and abbreviations which, unless the context otherwise
indicates or implies or unless otherwise specified, shall have the meanings as provided below. References to any statute,
legislation, act, regulation, rules, guidelines, clarifications, circulars, notifications, directions or policies or articles of
association or memorandum of association shall be to such statute, legislation, act, regulation, rules, guidelines, clarifications,
circulars, notifications, directions or policies or articles of association or memorandum of association as amended, updated,
supplemented, re-enacted or modified from time to time, and any reference to a statutory provision shall include any
subordinate legislation made from time to time under that provision. In case of any inconsistency between the definitions given
below and the definitions contained in the General Information Document, the definitions given below shall prevail.

The words and expressions used in this Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus – I but not defined herein shall have, to the
extent applicable, the same meanings ascribed to such terms under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, the SEBI Listing Regulations,
the SEBI Act, the Companies Act, the SCRA, the SCRR, the Depositories Act and the rules and regulations notified thereunder.
Further, the Offer related terms used but not defined in this Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus – I shall have the meanings
ascribed to such terms under the General Information Document (as defined hereinafter).

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the terms used in “Capital Structure”, “Objects of the Offer”, “Basis for Offer Price”,
“Statement of Special Tax Benefits”, “Industry Overview”, “Key Regulations and Policies in India”, “History and Certain
Corporate Matters”, “Restated Financial Information”, “Financial Indebtedness”, “Outstanding Litigation and Material

respectively, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the relevant section.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

Certain Non-GAAP financial measures relating to our financial performance, namely EBITDA, EBITDA Margin, PAT Margin,
Current Ratio, Net Capital Turnover Ratio, Return on Equity, and certain other industry metrics and financial parameters have
been included in this Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus – I. The presentation of these Non-GAAP Financial Measures is
not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance
with Ind-AS. We present these Non-GAAP Financial Measures because they are used by our management to evaluate our
operating performance and formulate business plans. Further, these Non-GAAP measures are not a measurement of our
financial performance or liquidity under Ind AS, Indian GAAP, or IFRS and should not be considered in isolation or construed
as an alternative to cash flows, profit / (loss) for the year / period or any other measure of financial performance or as an
indicator of our operating performance, liquidity, profitability or cash flows generated by operating, investing or financing
activities derived in accordance with Ind AS, Indian GAAP, or IFRS.

These Non-GAAP Financial Measures are not defined under Ind-AS and are not presented in accordance with Ind-AS. The
Non-GAAP Financial Measures have limitations as analytical tools. Further, these Non-GAAP Financial Measures may differ
from the similar information used by other companies, including industry peers, and therefore their comparability may be
limited. Therefore, these metrics should not be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to profit before tax or any
other measure of performance or as an indicator of our operating performance, liquidity or profitability or results of operations.
For further details, see “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations”, “Other
Financial Information” and “Risk Factors – 48. This Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus – I contains non-GAAP financial
measures and other selected statistical information related to our operations and financial performance. These non-GAAP

therefore may not be comparable with financial or statistical information of similar nomenclature computed and presented by
other industry peers.” on pages 323, 319, and 52, respectively.

2.   We are significantly dependent on our prepaid payment instruments (“PPIs”) program management and
     distribution business, the revenue from which represented 24.34%, 100.00%, 25.56%, 99.97% and 99.51% of our
     revenue from operations for the three months period ended June 30, 2026, the three months period ended June 30,
     2025 and the years ended March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and our Rewards and Loyalty business,
     which represented 69.80% of our revenue from operations for the three months period ended June 30, 2026, which
     was launched in second quarter of Fiscal 2026. If there is any decline in demand for the PPIs that we distribute or
     for our Rewards and Loyalty business, it could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition,
     results of operations and cash flows.

     We are a financial technology company focused on digital gifting, consumer spend management, and rewards and
     loyalty platforms. Our platforms comprise yayyy.shop (our direct-to-consumer (“D2C”) digital marketplace),
     SpendPro (a D2C spend management platform), and RewardOn (our business-to-business-to-consumer (“B2B2C”)
     rewards and loyalty platform), through which we have served 1,575,830 and 634,316 transacting users in India for
     Fiscal 2026 and the three months period ended June 30, 2026 respectively. We also offer technical & platform
     development services to businesses, which we have branded as “DevStack” (business-to-business “B2B”). For more
     details, see “Our Business – Our Products and Services” on page 227.

     We act as a program manager and business correspondent for non-reloadable prepaid payment instruments (“PPIs”)
     with a maximum value of ₹10,000 issued by banks and RBI licensed issuers (which we refer to as “PPI Issuers” and
     such PPIs, “Prepaid Cards”). We also act as a distribution agent to third-party program managers of Prepaid Cards.
     We refer to the third-party program managers of Prepaid Cards for whom we act as a distribution agent and the PPI
     Issuers for whom we act as a program manager as our “PPI Partners”. We also act as a distribution agent for
     aggregators of brand gift cards issued by merchants (which we refer to as “Gift Cards”). We refer to these activities
     as our “PPI Program Management and Distribution” business. We began distributing Gift Cards for aggregators
     of Gift Cards (“Gift Card Aggregators”) through our yayyy.shop website (our digital market place) in the second
     quarter of Fiscal 2026 and through our yayyy.shop mobile application in the fourth quarter of Fiscal 2026. We refer to
     our revenue from these activities as “Program Fees”.

     Our Rewards and Loyalty business comprises (i) reward points and our own reward points card, the “yayyy Reward
     Points Card”, which can be purchased directly through our digital marketplace on the yayyy.shop website and mobile
     application and used to redeem Gift Cards and Prepaid Cards available on the yayyy.shop website, and (ii) our
                                                                      21
RewardOn platform, a comprehensive, end-to-end digital rewards and incentives platform that enables corporate
customers to design, manage and distribute reward points to beneficiaries (users), which can be redeemed digitally
through a configurable rules engine integrated with a customised catalogue of Gift Cards, Prepaid Cards and the yayyy
Reward Points Card. Revenue from rewards points is recognised upon redemption of reward points for Gift
Cards/Prepaid Cards by users and the expiry of reward points, rather than at the time of sale of the reward points, and
is recorded on a gross basis.

As shown in the tables above, we derived 24.34%, 100.00%, 25.56%, 99.97% and 99.51% of our revenue from
operations for the three months period ended June 30, 2026, the three months period ended June 30, 2025 and Fiscals
2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively, from Program Fees and 69.80% and 68.68% of our revenue from operations for
the three months period ended June 30, 2026 and Fiscal 2026 from our Rewards and Loyalty business. Program Fees
are recognised on a net basis and revenue from our reward points business and Platform Fee / Service Fee are
recognised on a gross basis. Consequently, our reported revenue mix may not be indicative of the relative contribution
of each business line to our profitability, and a decline in Program Fees could have a disproportionate impact on our
margins and results of operations.

Our revenue from Program Fees primarily consists of (a) our share of interchange fees generated on spends on Prepaid
Cards at merchant outlets (at physical stores and online), comprising (i) our agreed share of the interchange fees with
the PPI Partners, and (ii) income from third-party service providers that provide transaction switching services to banks
in the form of incentives to promote issuer-specific programs and (b) commission income from Gift Card Aggregators
for facilitating the distribution of Gift Cards to users.

Interchange fees are decided by the payment networks of RuPay, Mastercard, and Visa (collectively, the “Payment
Networks”) in accordance with contractual arrangements between the Payment Networks and the PPI Issuers and is
broadly influenced by the industry of the merchant where the card is used, the merchant category and transaction value
(source: F&S Report, page 23). We have no influence on the interchange fee sharing structures and other commercial
terms determined by the Payment Networks and the PPI Issuers or the income from third-party service providers that
provide transaction switching services to banks. If there is a general decrease in interchange fees or a downward
revision in the incentives payable to us, it could have a material adverse effect on our PPI Program Management and
Distribution business and our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

We compete with other distributors of Prepaid Cards and Gift Cards, our PPI Partners and our Gift Card Aggregators,
and if we are unable to compete successfully it could have a material adverse effect on our PPI Program Management
and Distribution business and our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. For details on the
                                                                22
     competition faced by our PPI Program Management and Distribution business, see “– 29. We operate in a competitive
     business environment. Failure to compete effectively would have a material adverse effect on our business, financial
     condition, results of operations and cash flows” on page 45.

     Consumer adoption of digital gifting in India faces challenges due to a strong cultural preference for cash gifts, limited
     awareness outside metro cities, and concerns over sharing personal/payment data, while friction in delivery,
     redemption, or refunds—along with issues like expiry and unused balances—can reduce user satisfaction and impact
     engagement, especially for enterprise and loyalty programs (source: F&S Report, page 45). Any changes in consumer
     (user) or merchant preferences towards other non-cash payment methods, including debit cards and credit cards, could
     reduce demand for the Prepaid Cards and Gift Cards we distribute and for our Rewards and Loyalty business.

     The success of our Rewards and Loyalty business is also dependent, in part, on us having a broad and relevant
     catalogue of Gift Cards with commercially viable structures for redemption, as applicable. For more details, see “– 4.
     The success of our Rewards and Loyalty business is dependent, in part, on us having a broad and relevant catalogue
     of brand gift cards issued by merchants (Gift Cards) for redemption by users. As at June 30, 2026, we relied on three
     aggregators of Gift Cards (Gift Card Aggregators) and three dealers of Gift Cards (“Gift Card Dealers”) and their
     relationships with merchants or aggregators or aggregators or distributors of Gift Cards. If their commercial
     relationships with merchants are adversely affected or if one or more of those Gift Card Aggregators or Gift Card
     Dealers terminate their relationship with us and we were unable to find one or more alternative Gift Card Aggregators
     or Gift Card Dealers to replace them on commercially reasonable terms, it could decrease the range of Gift Cards we
     offer, thereby rendering our Gift Card catalogue less attractive to users, and adversely affect our revenue from our
     Rewards and Loyalty business. In addition, a shift in the redemption mix towards lower discount/margin Gift Cards,
     could reduce our revenue from our Rewards and Loyalty business” on page 24.

     terminate their relationship with us and we were unable to find one or more alternative Gift Card Aggregators or
     Gift Card Dealers to replace them on commercially reasonable terms, it could decrease the range of Gift Cards we
     offer, thereby rendering our Gift Card catalogue less attractive to users, and adversely affect our revenue from our
     Rewards and Loyalty business. In addition, a shift in the redemption mix towards lower discount/margin Gift Cards,
     could reduce our revenue from our Rewards and Loyalty business.

     The success of our Rewards and Loyalty business is dependent, in part, on us having a broad and relevant catalogue
     of brand gift cards issued by merchants (Gift Cards) for redemption by users. As at June 30, 2026, we had a catalogue
     of 234 Gift Cards across fashion, electronics, dining, travel, and e-commerce platforms, which are sourced from three
     Gift Card Aggregators and three Gift Card Dealers. Gift Card Aggregators are the distribution agents for the merchants
     who issue gift cards whereas Gift Card Dealers procure Gift Cards from Gift Card Aggregators and / or other Gift
     Card Distributors for onward distribution. These Gift Cards can be spent offline at the respective brand’s physical
     stores or online through the brand’s website or mobile application (if applicable). The corporate customers decide
     which Gift Cards we have available in our catalogue to make available for redemption by their respective beneficiaries
     (users) on the RewardOn platform.

     As at June 30, 2026, we had arrangements with three Gift Card Aggregators for the procurement of Gift Cards and
     also sourced Gift Cards from three Gift Card Dealers. The table below sets forth the number of Gift Cards available in
     each Gift Card Aggregator and Gift Card Dealer’s catalogue and the number of different Gift Cards we had available
     in our catalogue for redemption as at the date indicated:

     alternative Gift Card Aggregators or Gift Card Dealers to replace them on commercially reasonable terms, it could
     decrease the range of Gift Cards we offer, thereby rendering our Gift Card catalogue less attractive to users, and
     adversely affect our revenue from our Rewards and Loyalty business. Since we started our Rewards and Loyalty
     business in the second quarter of Fiscal 2026, there has been no instance of any of our Gift Card Aggregators or Gift
     Card Dealers terminating their agreement with us.

     Our revenue from the redemption of Gift Cards in exchange for reward points varies across brands and depends on (i)
     the commercial terms agreed between the respective Gift Card Aggregator or Gift Card Dealer and the merchants
     issuing the Gift Cards and (ii) the terms agreed upon between us and the respective Gift Card Aggregator or Gift Card
     Dealer. A shift in the redemption mix towards lower margin Gift Cards could reduce our revenue from our Rewards
     and Loyalty business and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

     As we scale our Rewards and Loyalty business, if Gift Card Aggregators or Gift Card Dealers are unable to supply us
     with the quantities of Gift Cards we need, it could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition,
     results of operations and cash flows.

     In addition, as at June 30, 2026, all three of our Gift Card Aggregators also operate direct-to-consumer and direct-to-
     channel distribution models and our three Gift Card Dealers also operate on a direct-to-channel distribution model.
     Any increased focus by such Gift Card Aggregators and Gift Card Dealers on their direct distribution channels may
     weaken our negotiating position, and adversely affect our transaction volumes and revenue earned and thereby have a
     material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

11.   Any disruption in the performance or availability of our technology infrastructure or the failure to integrate our
      offerings with application programming interfaces (APIs) and third-party platforms, or failure of third-party
      service providers to perform in combination with our internal infrastructure, could adversely affect customer and
      user experience, harm our reputation and have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition,
      results of operations and cash flows.

      Our business is heavily dependent on the uninterrupted performance and reliability of our technology platforms, which
      include SpendPro, RewardOn, and yayyy.shop, which are built on technology platforms conceptualised, designed and
      developed primarily in-house. Our technology platforms support processes for our PPI Partners and users of Prepaid
      Cards, our Gift Card Aggregators, Gift Card Dealers and users of Gift Cards, purchasers of reward points and
      beneficiaries of our rewards and loyalty programs. Any failure to deliver consistent system uptime or ensure high-
      speed access could result in dissatisfaction of users and corporate customers (in the case of RewardOn platform and
      DevStack), potential contract terminations and the payment of refunds to users. Further, our business is dependent on
      technology infrastructure, APIs (which is a set of rules, protocols, and tools that enables different software applications
      to communicate and share data) and third-party platforms, and any failure or disruption to this infrastructure could
      adversely affect our operations. Our operations, and the level of revenue generated, rely on the seamless integration
      with the technology systems of our Partners, vendors, and payment gateways. Any system failure, cybersecurity
      incident, data breach, API downtime or performance degradation could result in transaction failures, service
      interruptions, user dissatisfaction leading directly to the loss of revenue, and our business, financial condition, results
      of operations and cash flows could be adversely affected. We have obtained a cyber and data protection insurance policy
      which provides some third-party liability cover, including losses arising from data breaches, network security claims,
      regulatory costs and fines and e-payment / contractual penalties, as well as first-party cover for business interruption,
      including loss and restoration costs, as well as a hacker theft and cyber extortion cover. The coverage is limited and
      subject to exclusions, including for losses arising or attributable to third-party infrastructure or service providers.

      We rely on a combination of internal infrastructure and third-party service providers for the continuity of our
      operations. These include (i) cloud hosting service providers, (ii) internet service providers, (iii) payment processing
      services, and (iv) other technology and operational support systems. We purchase these products and services both
      directly from the service provider and also through licensed intermediaries under both long-term agreements and on a
      needs basis. For more details, see “Our Business – Third Party Service Providers” on page 233. We do not control
      these third-party systems and are dependent on their ongoing compatibility and support. If we are unable to integrate
      our offerings with such systems, or disruptions occur due to changes in technology, APIs, data formats, or commercial
      policies of these third parties, it could impair the functionality and utility of our offerings. Additionally, changes made
      to technology infrastructure without adequate coordination may lead to operational challenges or disruption of
      services. Further, our integration efforts may be impacted by errors, delays, or quality issues whether on our part or
      that of our Partners, Gift Card Aggregators, Gift Card Dealers, vendors, and payment gateways, and such other
      integration partners required for our business operations. Inappropriate modification of data, failure to maintain data
      integrity, or security breaches by third-party systems could compromise our service delivery and result in user
      dissatisfaction, reputational damage, and potential liability. Integration-related costs, including development,
      maintenance, monitoring and remediation expenses, may increase over time and could adversely affect margins if such
      costs cannot be recovered through increases in pricing. Our systems and the systems of third-party service providers
      are susceptible to internal factors, such as software bugs, system errors, hardware failures, capacity limitations, and
      integration issues, and external factors, such as cyber-attacks, denial-of-service incidents, and cloud infrastructure
      failures. Since April 1, 2023, we have not experienced any material failures of performance or availability of our
      technology infrastructure or the failure of third-party service providers to perform the services needed to operate our
      business and there have been no material failures of integration between our systems and third-party systems,
      applications, and tools.

      In addition, our third-party service providers could seek to terminate their agreements with us or restrict our access to
      their goods/services. If such instances occur and we are unable to transition to alternative providers on commercially
      reasonable terms in a timely manner, our service levels could be adversely affected, leading to potential loss of
      customers and users, reputational harm, and adverse effects on our financial condition, results of operations and cash
      flows. Since April 1, 2023, there have been no such instances.

12.   We rely on the seamless operation and systems of the banks and RBI licensed issuers whose prepaid instruments

13.   Any security breaches of our information technology systems or data breaches or failure to comply with relevant
      data protection or privacy laws could have a material adverse effect on our reputation, business, financial condition,
      results of operations and cash flows.

      We collect information from users of our products, including personally identifiable information, such as a verified
      mobile number and a self-declaration. As such, we face risks relating to compliance with laws, rules and regulations
      relating to the collection, storage, use, sharing, disclosure, protection and security of personal information of users. In
      India, these laws, rules and regulations include the Information Technology Act, 2000 and rules thereunder and the
      Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (“DPDP Act”) (which received the assent of the President on August 11,
      2023 and is being enforced in a phased manner from November 14, 2025). The DPDP Act provides for personal data
      protection and privacy of individuals, regulates cross-border data transfer, and provides several exemptions for
      personal data processing by the Government. The DPDP Act provides for and imposes restrictions and obligations on
      data fiduciaries resulting from dealing with personal data and provides for levy of penalties for breach of obligations
      prescribed under the DPDP Act. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India
      notified the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (“DPDP Rules”) on November 14, 2025. The DPDP Rules
      shall come into force on various dates, ranging from the date of publication to 18 months after the date of publication.
      The DPDP Rules provide detailed rules for data fiduciaries, consent managers, and the Data Protection Board to ensure
      compliance with the DPDP Act. For further details, see “Key Regulations and Policies in India” on page 238.

      Any security breach, material disruption of, or damage to, our operational systems, or data processing activities, or the
      systems of our integration partners could result in a loss of confidence in the security of our products and services and
      damage to our brands, reduce the demand for our products and services, disrupt our operations, result in the exfiltration
      of proprietary data and information, including source code, require us to spend material resources to investigate or
      correct the breach and to prevent future security breaches and incidents, and expose us to legal liabilities on account
      of our failure to comply with contractual obligations relating to security breaches or comply with applicable data
      security and privacy laws and could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of
      operations and cash flows.

      We have obtained a cyber and data protection insurance policy which provides some third-party liability cover,
      including losses arising from data breaches, network security claims, regulatory costs and fines and e-payment /
      contractual penalties, as well as first-party cover for business interruption, including loss and restoration costs, as well
      as hacker theft and cyber extortion cover. The coverage is limited and subject to exclusions, including for losses arising
      or attributable to third-party infrastructure or service providers. Since April 1, 2023, we have not been subject to any
      instances of security or data breaches or failed to comply with applicable laws, rules and regulations relating to the
      collection, storage, use, sharing, disclosure, protection and security of personal information.

      •        Inability to successfully manage growth;

15.   We depend on internet search engines, mobile operating systems and application marketplaces to drive traffic to
      our yayyy.shop platform. If we do not effectively operate with or receive favourable placements within such engines
      and operating systems our business, financial results, cash flows and results of operations could be adversely
      affected.

      Our ability to attract users (consumers) through unpaid internet search results on search engines affects our business,
      financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. The number of users of Prepaid Cards and Gift Cards we
      attract to our yayyy.shop website from search engines is due, in large part, to our yayyy.shop website rankings in
      unpaid search results, which are not under our direct control and may change frequently, such as, a change in a search
      engine ranking algorithms resulting in reduction of the traffic to our websites. In addition, our competitors may be
      ranked higher and be able to attract more users through search results, decreasing the discoverability of the Prepaid
      Cards and Gift Cards we distribute. As a result, any reduction in the number of users directed to our yayyy.shop website
      could adversely affect the success of our PPI Program Management and Distribution business. Any sustained reduction
      in traffic from unpaid search results may require us to increase spending on paid advertising and promotional channels,
      which could increase our brand & business promotion expenses and thereby adversely affect our margins and
      profitability.

      We also depend on the well-known mobile operating system and a well-known application marketplace to make our
      yayyy.shop mobile application available. Therefore, failure to adhere to any changes in such operating system and/or
      policy of such application store could adversely affect the availability of our yayyy.shop mobile application. If such
      mobile operating system or application marketplace limits or prohibits us from making our yayyy.shop mobile
      application available, make changes that degrade the functionality of our yayyy.shop mobile application, impose terms
      of use unsatisfactory to us, or modify their search or ratings algorithms in ways that are detrimental to us, or if our
      competitors’ placement in such mobile operating systems’ application marketplace is more prominent than the
      placement of our yayyy.shop mobile application, the growth in the number of our total transacting users could slow
      down.

      User ratings, reviews and feedback on application marketplaces or online platforms may significantly influence user
      perception and download decisions, and any increase in negative reviews or ratings, whether justified or not, could
                                                              32
      adversely affect our brands and growth. Adverse changes in ratings and reviews or decreased visibility metrics on
      mobile applications marketplaces could materially affect download volumes and user trust. In addition, our mobile
      application may also experience technological glitches in the future. Our mobile application was released in the fourth
      quarter of Fiscal 2026 and has not experienced any material technological glitches to date.

      As new mobile devices and mobile platforms are released, there is no guarantee that such upgrades will continue to
      support our yayyy.shop application or effectively roll out updates to our application. In addition, we need to ensure
      that our yayyy.shop application is designed to perform with a range of mobile technologies. Further, the introduction
      of new operating systems would require us to adapt and/ or adjust our yayyy.shop mobile application with their
      technology, which could entail significant cost and resources. If users encounter any difficulty accessing or using our
      yayyy.shop mobile application on their mobile devices or if we are unable to adapt to changes in the mobile operating
      system on which our yayyy.shop mobile application is made available, the growth in the number of our total transacting
      users could slow down and thereby adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash
      flows.

21.   If we are unable to adequately protect our intellectual property, it could have a material adverse effect on our
      business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

      Our intellectual property is an essential asset of our business. As on the date of this Updated Draft Red Herring
      Prospectus-I, our Company has made 25 trademark applications under various classes in India under the Trade Marks
      Act, 1999, including our Company’s name, and the names and logos of “SpendPro”, “RewardOn” and “yayyy” which
      are pending at various stages.

      Further, our Company has two registered trademarks in India for “Paramotor” logo under classes 9 and 36 of the Trade
      Marks Act, 1999. Our Company has applied for three copyrights in respect of the computer software titled
      “RewardOn”, “SpendPro” and “yayyy” under the Copyright Act, 1957, which are currently pending.

      For more details on our registered trademarks and copyrights, see “Our Business – Intellectual Property” and
      “Government and Other Approvals – V. Intellectual Property Rights” on pages 233 and 368, respectively. In the
      absence of these trademarks, we may not be able to initiate an infringement action against any infringing third-party.
      With respect to our trademarks and copyrights that have been applied for and/or any that may be objected to or opposed,
      we cannot assure you that we will be successful in such a challenge, nor can we provide any assurance that such
      trademarks and copyrights will be granted. As a result, we may not be able to prevent infringement of our trademarks
      and copyrights and a passing-off action may not provide sufficient protection until such time that such registration is
      granted.

      A registered trademark in India has a validity period of 10 years from the date of registration, which can be renewed
      from time-to-time to maintain continuous protection for a period of 10 years from the date of expiration of the prior
      registration. The renewal of a trademark is entirely under the control of the holder, and we intend to renew our
      trademarks before they expire unless we are no longer using them or circumstances beyond our control leading to late
      renewals.

      Our websites rely on in-house customizations and enhancements of third-party technology, much of which is not
      subject to intellectual property protection which may limit our ability to prevent competitors from replicating our
      offerings. The renewal of domain names is entirely under the control of the holder, and we intend to renew the
      registration of our domain names before they expire unless we are no longer using them. Other parties could create an
      alternative domain name resembling ours that could be passed off as one of our domain names.

      Agreements entered into with our employees, customers or third parties that receive access to our proprietary or
      confidential information typically include confidentiality clauses. No assurance can be given that these agreements
      will be effective in controlling access to or the distribution of our proprietary information. Further, these agreements
      will not prevent potential competitors from independently developing technologies that may be substantially
      equivalent to or superior to ours.

      If we are unable to adequately protect our intellectual property rights, our business could be adversely affected, as
      third parties may be able to commercialize and use a brand that is substantially the same as ours to compete with us
      without incurring the development and branding costs that we have incurred. Any of our intellectual property rights
      could be challenged, invalidated, circumvented, infringed, misappropriated or violated, or could be disclosed in an
      unauthorized manner to third parties. Any enforcement efforts we undertake, including litigation, could be time-
      consuming and expensive, could divert management’s attention and could result in a court determining that our
      intellectual property rights are unenforceable. If we are unsuccessful in protecting our intellectual property rights, it
                                                             38
      could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. Since
      April 1, 2023, there have been no instances of unauthorised use of our intellectual property.

22.   If we are unable to obtain, renew or maintain the statutory permits, approvals and licenses necessary for the
      operation of our business, our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects could be materially
      and adversely affected.

      In the course of our business operations in India, we are required to obtain various approvals, licenses, registrations,
      authorizations and permits, and make necessary registrations and notice filings with governmental, statutory and
      regulatory authorities. Given the dynamic nature of regulatory frameworks in India, we may also need to obtain
      additional licenses and approvals as new regulations are enacted. There are no material approvals pending in relation
      to our business and operations. For details, see “Government and Other Approvals” on page 367.

      The licenses, authorizations, and approvals we have obtained are subject to various conditions. We cannot guarantee
      our ability to continuously fulfil such conditions, and there can be no assurance that the government or other regulatory
      bodies will not impose onerous requirements and conditions on our operations. Non-compliance with the conditions
      of the licenses, authorizations or approvals may lead to their cancellation, revocation, or suspension. In addition, if we
      were found to be in violation of applicable licensing requirements by a court or a state, federal, or local enforcement
      agency, or agree to resolve such concerns by voluntary agreement, we could be subject to or required to pay fines,
      damages, injunctive relief (including required modification or discontinuation of our business in certain areas),
      criminal penalties, and other penalties or consequences. While we have not faced any such material instances since
      April 1, 2023, however, if we fail to seek or obtain the requisite permits, approvals and licenses, or if our existing
      permits, approvals and licenses are withdrawn by the relevant authority, our ability to maintain business operations
      and execute our objectives as planned could be compromised, thereby adversely affecting our business, financial
      condition, results of operations and cash flows.

23.   Our insurance coverage may be inadequate to protect us against all potential losses, which could have an adverse
      effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. In particular, we have not obtained
      insurance policies to cover us for losses resulting from business interruption, commercial general liability except
      to the extent covered by our cyber and data protection insurance, and any such losses would have to be borne by
      us, which could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

      We have obtained a burglary insurance policy in respect of computer and computer equipment and office equipment
      at each of our offices, and a Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha insurance policy in respect of computer and computer
      equipment, furniture, fixtures and fittings, and office equipment at each of our offices. The Bharat Sookshma Udyam
      Suraksha insurance excludes losses caused by labour unrest, deprivation of use or value of property due to actions by
      any government authority, and damages caused by chemical or biological contaminants. The burglary insurance policy
      provides for exclusions such as larceny and terrorism. We have obtained a cyber and data protection insurance policy
      which covers third-party liability including privacy and data breaches, network security claims, media liability claims,
      regulatory costs and fines, e-payment / contractual penalties, as well as first party business interruption and crime
      coverage, such as business interruption loss and restoration costs, and hacker theft and cyber extortion. The policy
      provides for exclusions including losses in connection to third-party infrastructure or service providers, infringement,
      misappropriation, dilution, misuse or inducement to infringe, misappropriate, dilute or misuse any patent or patent right,
      any bodily injury or material damage losses, financial market or trading losses, war, terrorism, governmental acts, prior
      claims and other circumstances as per policy wordings. We have obtained a vehicle policy which covers risks arising
      from the use of the insured vehicle, including self-caused damage to the vehicle and third-party liability involving the
      vehicle, subject to the terms, conditions, and exclusions and limits of the policy. For details on our offices, see “Our
      Business – Properties” on page 235. We have also obtained a Directors and Officers Liability Insurance policy and
      provide comprehensive health insurance coverage to our employees under a group policy. For details of our insurance
      policies, see “Our Business – Insurance” on page 234. We have not obtained insurance policies to cover other potential
      risks and liabilities, such as for business interruption, commercial general liability, except to the extent covered by our
      cyber and data protection insurance and any such losses would have to be borne by us, which could have a material
      adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

25.   Misconduct by our employees could adversely affect our reputation, business, financial condition, results of
      operations and cash flows.

      We are exposed to the risk of misconduct by our employees. Such misconduct may include fraudulent activities,
      misrepresentation or mis-selling, unauthorized use or disclosure of confidential or proprietary information,
      manipulation of customer data, breaches of contractual obligations, or infringement of third-party intellectual property
      rights. These actions could result in regulatory scrutiny, legal liabilities, reputational damage and financial loss. Fraud
      and the mis-selling of Prepaid Cards by our Company, our employees and agents could also expose us to penalty
      payments for the misused value, which may be due to a PPI Partner. Misconduct by key managerial personnel or
      employees in critical technology, operations or compliance roles could have a disproportionate adverse effect on our
      business due to their influence over systems and decision-making. We have implemented various safeguards to
      mitigate such risks, including a structured onboarding and background verification process, internal access control
      protocols, periodic employee training, a whistleblower mechanism, and a vigilance committee. Since April 1, 2023,
      there has been no material instance of employee misconduct. However, there can be no assurance that these controls
      will be effective in all cases or that we will be able to respond to instances of misconduct by our employees in an
      adequate or timely manner, or at all. Any such instance of misconduct by our employees could adversely affect our
      reputation, business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

      There is also a risk that current or former employees may use our proprietary knowledge, systems, or customer
      relationships to launch competing businesses. Since April 1, 2023, there has been no instance of any of our current or
      former employees having used our proprietary knowledge, systems, or customer relationships to launch competing
      businesses.

26.   The incidence of fraudulent transactions could lead to negative publicity, reputational damage and losses.

      Prepaid Cards, Gift Cards, yayyy Reward Points Cards and rewards points are susceptible to fraud, including phishing,
      account compromise, unauthorized redemption and misuse by users or intermediaries. Prepaid Cards present a higher
      risk of fraud due to their usability at any merchant that accepts cards on the applicable payment network, while Gift
      Cards may be vulnerable to bulk purchases, arbitrage or unauthorised secondary market distribution. Fraudulent
      transactions could arise from failures or vulnerabilities in third-party systems, including those of our PPI Partners,
      payment networks, Gift Card Aggregators and Gift Card Dealers that we integrate with, and we may nevertheless be
      required to absorb losses arising from such incidents. Fraud incidents involving third-party systems that we are
      integrated with may negatively affect user trust in our platforms. Under our agreement with one of our PPI Partners,
      we are liable to indemnify this Partner against liability, losses, costs and expenses arising out of any act, omission,
      commission, negligence, fraud, forgery, dishonesty, misconduct or violation of any terms and conditions of the
      agreement by our Company or our personnel. In addition, pursuant to our agreement with another of our PPI Partners,
      we are liable to pay this Partner a penalty of up to 10% of the mis-used value of Prepaid Cards for every instance of
      fraud and the mis-selling of Prepaid Cards by us, our employees or agents. While we have not experienced any
      fraudulent transactions in the three months period ended June 30, 2026 or June 30, 2025 or Fiscals 2026, 2025 or 2024,
      the incidence of fraud, even if financial losses are limited, involving Prepaid Cards, Gift Cards, yayyy Reward Points
                                                                      41
      Cards or rewards points could adversely affect user trust in our business and our reputation could be damaged, which
      could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

27.   Issues related to the development and use of artificial intelligence could give rise to legal and/or regulatory action,
      damage our reputation or otherwise materially harm our business. The integration of artificial intelligence in our
      tools and platforms also exposes us to additional data security and privacy risks.

      We plan to continue to invest in artificial intelligence (“AI”) / machine learning (“ML”) based capabilities by investing
      in (i) scalable cloud and compute infrastructure to enable faster deployment and scaling of agentic tools, (ii)
      strengthening model research and ML operations frameworks to enhance the reliability, security and governance of
      automated systems, and (iii) undertaking focused investments in talent acquisition and upskilling to improve
      productivity and operating leverage. In parallel, we intend to deepen the use of AI-driven fraud detection and
      compliance solutions to reduce loss rates, strengthen risk controls and try to ensure the responsible and safe deployment
      of AI across our digital gifting ecosystem. For more details, see “Our Business – Our Strategies – Enhance our
      technology and infrastructure” on page 224.

      Our increasing reliance on AI-enabled tools across fraud detection, compliance and platform operations exposes us to
      operational, regulatory and reputational risks. AI algorithms and training methodologies may produce inaccurate,
      biased, incomplete or non-explainable outputs. Errors or unintended outcomes could lead to commercial losses,
      customer disputes or reputational harm. While we aim to develop and use AI responsibly and attempt to identify and
      mitigate ethical and legal issues presented by its use, we may be unsuccessful in identifying or resolving issues before
      they arise. Developing, deploying and maintaining AI-enabled solutions may require significant investment in
      technology, talent and compliance capabilities, and there can be no assurance that such investments will result in
      proportionate commercial benefits.

      Integrating AI poses significant data privacy and security risks. We hold a cyber and data protection insurance policy
      that would provide some coverage against losses resulting from third-party liability including privacy and data breach,
      network security claims, cybersecurity incidents, first party business interruption and certain other special perils,
      subject to exclusions. The coverage is limited and subject to exclusions, including those relating to third-party services
      or infrastructure used by our Company. Moreover, staying compliant with evolving laws, regulations, and industry
      standards pertaining to AI may impose significant operational costs and constrain our ability to develop, deploy, or
      employ AI technologies. Failing to adapt appropriately to this evolving regulatory environment could result in legal
      liability, regulatory actions, and damage to our brand and reputation. There have been certain initiatives undertaken
      by government agencies in India regarding the regulation of AI, including the India AI Governance Guidelines,
      unveiled by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology in November 2025 under the IndiaAI Mission,
      which was launched in 2024. The India AI Governance Guidelines outline the governance initiatives to support safe
      and responsible AI adoption and to foster innovation, alongside broader mission measures on compute, datasets and
      safety. These initiatives also emphasise reviewing existing laws to address potential gaps in areas such as classification
      and liability across the AI value chain, the application of data protection principles to AI development, the misuse of
      generative AI and challenges around content authentication/provenance, the use of copyrighted material in training,
      and sector specific risks.

     During Fiscal 2024, our Company had received a Show Cause Notice (“SCN”) towards GST demand amounting to ₹ 30.52 million, along
     with interest of ₹ 33.27 million and a penalty of ₹ 3.06 million from Jurisdictional Dy. Commissioner of State Tax. Our Company submitted
     the relevant explanation in response to said SCN. On April 26, 2024, the Jurisdictional Dy. Commissioner of State Tax passed an order
     demanding GST of ₹ 30.52 million, along with interest of ₹ 33.27 million and a penalty of ₹3.06 million. Our Company filed an appeal before
     the Joint Commissioner of State Tax (Appeal-VI), Mumbai on July 10, 2024, along with a pre-deposit amount of ₹ 3.05 million. The Joint
     Commissioner of State Tax passed an appeal order dated August 14, 2025 of demand of tax of ₹ 0.03 million, interest of ₹ 0.04 million and a
     penalty of ₹0.01 million, aggregating to ₹ 0.09 million. Our Company has given the effect of said tax demand in its financial statements for
     Fiscal 2026. Despite the order of the Jurisdictional Dy. Commissioner of State Tax passed on April 26, 2024 and the fact that our Company
     has already made a pre-deposit amount of ₹ 3.05 million, the website https://payment.gst.gov.in/payment/auth/ledger/paymenttowardsdemand
     shows that our Company still owes ₹ 0.03 million in relation to this SCN. Therefore, this ₹ 0.03 million has been considered to still be in
     dispute.

29.   We operate in a competitive business environment. Failure to compete effectively would have a material adverse
      effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

      There are significant barriers to entry to distribute Prepaid Cards, as onboarding of distributors by PPI Partners
      typically involves rigorous empanelment and due diligence processes encompassing compliance, technology, and
      operational assessments (source: F&S Report, page 25). Becoming a scaled program manager in India is difficult
      because it combines regulated ecosystem access with operational excellence (source: F&S Report, page 25). Wallets,
      neo-banks, and big fintech apps can replicate budgeting / alerts features on top of bank accounts, raising competition
      for attention and reducing differentiation unless the prepaid-linked control layer is compelling (source: F&S Report,
      page 25). Other prominent players operating in the Prepaid Card Distribution space in India include Happay,
      OmniCard, Zaggle and Volopay (source: F&S Report, page 16).

      India’s digital gift card market is highly competitive and increasingly saturated, with fintechs, digital wallets, e-
      commerce platforms, banks, loyalty companies, and unorganized players all offering similar gifting solutions (source:
      F&S Report, page 45). This intense competition makes differentiation difficult, while large platforms can bundle
      gifting into broader ecosystems, reducing pricing power for standalone players (source: F&S Report, page 45). At the
      same time, price-sensitive consumers and enterprise buyers negotiate aggressively, leading to margin pressure,
      especially when combined with payment gateway fees and seasonal discounting (source: F&S Report, page 45).
      Prominent players in the digital Gift Card market include Pine Labs Limited (operates Woohoo), Vouchagram India
      Private Limited (operates GyFTR) and Parity Cube Private Limited (operates Zingoy) (source: F&S Report, page 45).

      Prominent players in the Rewards & Loyalty Market include Capillary Technologies India Limited, Zaggle Prepaid
      Ocean Services Limited, Easyrewardz Software Services Private Limited, Edenred (India) Private Limited, Nreach
      Online Services Private Limited (operates Xoxoday / Plum / Empuls), and Thriwe Consulting Private Limited
      (erstwhile GolfLan Technology Solutions Private Limited) (source: F&S Report, page 29).

      Prominent players operating in the custom fintech software development include Saksoft Limited, Aurionpro Solutions
      Limited, InfoBeans Technologies Limited and Datamatics Global Services Limited (source: F&S Report, page 47).

      In addition, we have a limited history of operating our Rewards and Loyalty business, which we launched in the second
      quarter of Fiscal 2026, and DevStack business, which was launched in the first quarter of Fiscal 2026. For more details,
      see “– 1. We launched our dedicated technical and platform development services (DevStack) in the first quarter of
      Fiscal 2026 and we launched our Rewards and Loyalty business, which includes reward points sold via our yayyy
      Reward Points Cards and our RewardOn platform, in the second quarter of Fiscal 2026. Our limited experience in
      offering these products and services could adversely affect our ability to scale these businesses efficiently. We had six
      and five corporate customers using the RewardOn platform for the three months period ended June 30, 2026 and
      Fiscal 2026, respectively. We had five customers for our DevStack business as at June 30, 2026” on page 20.

      Some of our current and potential competitors may have longer operating histories, higher brand recognition, stronger
      and more extensive partner relationships, significantly greater financial, technical, marketing, and other resources,
      lower labour and development costs, and larger customer bases than we do. These competitors may invest and engage
      in more extensive research and development (R&D) efforts and thereby develop better technology than what we
      currently use. They may also undertake more far-reaching promotions and adopt more aggressive pricing policies that
      will allow them to build larger customer bases than we have. Furthermore, our current and potential competitors may
      make acquisitions or enter into strategic relationships and rapidly acquire significant market share due to a larger
      customer base, superior product offering, more effective sales and marketing operations, or greater financial, technical,
      and other resources.

      Competitive pressure could result in price reductions, the loss of customers, increased customer concentration risk and
      reduced margins, which could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations
      and cash flows.

      For details on operational and financial benchmarking for us and our competitors in India, see “Industry Overview –
      Financial & Operational KPIs” on page 200. In addition, for details in relation to a comparison of our KPIs with our
      listed industry peers, see “Basis for Offer Price – Comparison with listed industry peers” on page 129.

30.   Our revenue from operations has historically been higher in the second half of a fiscal year (third and fourth
      quarters) compared to the first half two quarters of a fiscal year (first and second quarters). Consequently, any
      decrease in demand for our products and services during the third and fourth quarters of a fiscal year could have
      a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operation and cash flows for that fiscal year.

      We have historically experienced higher revenue from operations in the second half of a fiscal year (third and fourth
      quarters) compared to the first half (first and second quarters), with revenue from operations in the second half ranging
                                                            45
      between approximately 55% to 75% of our total annual revenue from operations, as compared to approximately 25%
      to 45% in the first half for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, based on the Company’s unaudited financial statements for
      the interim periods. The third quarter of a fiscal year encompasses holidays such as Dusshera, Diwali and Christmas,
      with corresponding higher payment transaction volumes before and during these festivals. Retailers have end of season
      sales and end of financial year sales in the fourth quarter of a fiscal year, with corresponding higher payment
      transaction volumes. Our results of operations for the third and fourth quarters of a fiscal year may not be indicative
      of our results of operations for the first two quarters and such seasonality can be expected to cause fluctuations in our
      results of operations.

      During times of increased seasonal demand, it is possible that a large number of customers may attempt to access our
      technology platforms within a short period of time, which may cause us to experience system interruptions that result
      in our technology platforms temporarily being unavailable. Failure to meet demand associated with the seasonality
      may materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. Since April
      1, 2023, no instance of our inability to meet seasonal demand has occurred.

      Further, lower than expected revenue from operations during the third and fourth quarters of a fiscal year could have
      a disproportionate adverse effect on our results of operations for any fiscal year.

      Our results of operations for a given quarter may not be necessarily indicative of our results of operations for other
      quarters.

      We face risks relating to compliance with laws, rules and regulations relating to the collection, storage, use, sharing,
      disclosure, protection and security of personal information. In India, these laws, rules and regulations include the
      Information Technology Act, 2000 and rules thereunder and the DPDP Act. We hold an insurance policy that would
      cover us for some losses resulting from third-party liability including privacy and data breach, network security claims,
      cybersecurity incidents, first party business interruption and certain other special perils. However, such coverage is
      limited and subject to exclusions, including those relating to third-party infrastructure or services used by our
      Company. For more details, see “– 13. Any security breaches of our information technology systems or data breaches
      or failure to comply with relevant data protection or privacy laws could have a material adverse effect on our
      reputation, business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows” and “Key Regulations and Policies in
      India” and “Our Business – Insurance” on pages 31, 238 and 234, respectively.

      Additionally, our business is also subject to various central, state and local laws, including employment and labour
      laws, workplace safety, consumer protection laws, anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws, intellectual property laws,
      and tax laws and regulations. For details of certain sector specific laws and regulations in India that are applicable to
      us, see “Key Regulations and Policies in India” on page 238.

      While we attempt to ensure compliance with the applicable laws and regulations relating to our business, we cannot
      assure you that the Government or the regulatory authorities will not take different interpretations regarding
      applicability of, or compliance with, the laws and regulatory framework governing our business. Any failure or alleged
      failure to comply with the applicable laws, regulations or requirements could subject us to enforcement actions by the
      relevant authority.

      We could be adversely affected if legislations or regulations are expanded or amended to require changes in our
      business practices, or if such legislations or regulations are interpreted or implemented in ways that negatively affect
      our business. Non-compliance with applicable regulations or requirements could subject us to investigations,
      enforcement actions, and sanctions, mandatory changes to our network and products, disgorgement of profits, fines,
      and damages, civil and criminal penalties or injunctions, claims for damages by our customers or business
      collaboration partners and termination of contracts. Since April 1, 2023, we have not been subject to any regulatory
      actions for failing to comply with applicable laws and regulations relating to our business.

32.   The issuance, distribution and usage of prepaid payment instruments (“PPIs”) are regulated by the Reserve Bank
      of India (“RBI”) and any change in the RBI’s policies, decisions and regulatory framework in relation to PPIs
      could adversely affect our business, cash flows, results of operations and financial condition.

      The issuance, distribution and usage of Prepaid Cards and Gift Cards are regulated by the RBI pursuant to the Payment
      and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 and the Master Directions issued by RBI in 2021 in relation to Prepaid Payment
      Instruments, as updated. Although we do not issue Prepaid Cards, the PPI Issuers for whom we act as a program
      manager or distribution agent are regulated by the RBI, and we are, therefore, indirectly subject to regulatory
      requirements relating to, among other things, KYC, AML, interoperability, data localisation requirements, and usage
      restrictions and reporting.

      The introduction of new laws or regulations in relation to PPIs by the RBI could adversely affect our business, financial
                                                            46
      condition and results of operations. Any regulatory restrictions on outsourcing, program management arrangements,
      or third-party participation in PPI issuance could adversely affect our ability to operate as a program manager or
      distributor. Regulatory measures affecting permitted use cases, loading limits, merchant categories or transaction types
      for PPIs could restrict the features, functionality or commercial viability of Prepaid Cards/ Gift Cards distributed by
      us. Increased capital, liquidity or compliance requirements imposed on PPI issuers/ Gift Card issuers could adversely
      affect their willingness or ability to continue or expand partnerships with us on commercially viable terms. Compliance
      with new regulations governing issuers of PPIs and issuers of Gift Card could also result in significant expenditure for
      them that could cause them to renegotiate or terminate existing agreements, or curtail their operations, which could
      adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. Furthermore, any adverse
      regulatory action that changes a PPI Issuer’s business or adversely affects its financial condition or results of
      operations, may adversely affect our partnership with such PPI Issuer, thereby adversely affecting our business,
      financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. Changes in customer KYC or transaction monitoring
      requirements applicable to PPI Issuers or program managers of Prepaid Cards could increase onboarding friction,
      reduce user conversions and adversely affect transaction volumes. Since April 1, 2023, there have not been any changes
      in regulations relating to PPIs or their interpretation or enforcement that have had a material adverse effect on our
      business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.

      Any suspension, cancellation of license, penalty or any other adverse regulatory action against any PPI Issuers whose
      Prepaid Cards we distribute could disrupt the supply of Prepaid Cards, reduce user confidence, cause reputational harm
      and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. Since April 1, 2023, there
      have not been any material instances of the foregoing.

      Currently, interchange fees on Prepaid Cards are not subject to any regulatory caps. However, the RBI has
      implemented regulations limiting interchange fees payable on debit card transactions, including the ceiling on the
      merchant discount rate applicable for debit card transactions, and if any similar regulations are extended to Prepaid
      Cards in the future it could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations
      and cash flows. Further, the National Payments Corporation of India has implemented limits on merchant discount
      rate (“MDR”) fees applicable on UPI transactions paid by merchants to banks and payment service providers, which
      includes interchange fees.

      Although we are not regulated by the RBI, the RBI may in the future introduce requirements applicable to program
      managers and distributors of PPIs, which could increase our compliance burden, restrict certain activities or require
      changes to our business model.

      of operations and cash flows may be adversely affected.

      While we take measures to ensure that we do not infringe upon the intellectual property rights of others, such as
      intellectual property clearance checks prior to the launch of a product/brand and controls for the use of third-party
      content, we cannot determine with certainty as to whether we are infringing any existing third-party intellectual
      property rights which may force us to obtain licences or cease some of our operations. We may also be susceptible to
      claims from third parties asserting infringement and other related claims. If claims or actions are asserted against us,
      we may be subject to costly litigation or may be required to obtain a licence or modify our offerings. Such licences or
      modifications could be extremely costly. Further, necessary licences may not be available to us on satisfactory terms,
      if at all. In addition, we may decide to settle a claim or action against us, which could be costly. We may also be liable
      for any past infringement. An inadvertent breach or any misuse of intellectual property or proprietary data by any of
      our employees or sub-contractors may expose us to expensive infringement claims. The occurrence of any of the
      foregoing in the future could adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
      Since April 1, 2023, we have not experienced any claims in relation to the infringement of intellectual property rights.
      However, we cannot assure you that there will be no such instances in the future.

      require the Net Proceeds to meet any other expenditure or fund any exigencies arising out of the competitive
