5.7   Value Chain and stakeholder ecosystem

      India’s digital gift card market operates through a well-integrated, tech-driven value chain, connecting issuers, aggregators,
      platforms, and end consumers. The ecosystem leverages massive fintech and digital infrastructure, with prominent players
      driving both B2C and B2B growth.

      1.         Issuers (Content/Product Creators): Brands and retailers create gift products, vouchers, and prepaid solutions:

                 •          Brands: FMCG (chocolates, flowers), electronics, lifestyle, apparel, and wellness (e.g., Amazon,
                            Flipkart, Wow! Momo, ChocoCraft).

                 •          Retailers: Physical and online stores offering their own vouchers and products.

      2.      Aggregators & Distributors (Tech Backbone): These entities manage issuance, fulfilment, and technology:

              •        Gift Card Platforms: yayyy.shop, Pine Labs Ltd.(Woohoo), Gyftr

              •        FinTechs & Payment Gateways: Razorpay, PayU, banks ensuring secure transactions and escrow.

              •        E-commerce Platforms: Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra integrating digital gifting into their offerings.

      3.      Platforms & Channel Partners (Sales & Usage Layer): They enable purchase, redemption, and corporate
              deployment:

              •        E-commerce Marketplaces: Selling curated gift hampers and digital vouchers.

              •        Incentive & Loyalty Programs: Digital gifts used for CRM, partner, and customer rewards, including

                       deployment through a modular, API-driven platform.

      4.      Technology & Infrastructure:

              •        Cloud Solutions: Ensure scalability and reliability for platforms.

              •        AI & Personalization: Customizing gifting experiences.

              •        Secure Payment Systems: RBI-regulated entities maintain trust and transaction security.

      5.      End Consumers & Recipients:

              •        B2C: Individuals purchasing gifts for personal use and gifting.

              •        B2B: Employees, channel partners, and customers receiving corporate rewards and incentives.

              This multi-layered ecosystem efficiently connects product creation, distribution, and consumption, enabling a
              fast-growing, scalable, and tech-driven digital gifting market in India.

5.8   Business model / Revenue model

      In India’s digital gift card ecosystem, revenue models are hybrid and multi-layered, combining commission-based income,
      white-label/API-driven B2B licensing, and deep integration into rewards, loyalty, and spend programmes. Players cater to
      banks, fintechs, FMCG brands, enterprises, and e-commerce platforms, offering digital gift cards, vouchers, and wallets
      as core products.

      1.      Commission-Based Revenue Model: This is the foundational model for most digital gifting platforms. This
              model is best suited for marketplaces, consumer gifting platforms, and aggregator models.

              Revenue Sources

              i.       Transaction Fees: A percentage commission on the sale or redemption value of digital gift cards and
                       vouchers, common in e-commerce, food delivery, and retail partnerships.

              ii.      Merchant Commissions: Brands pay commissions when customers redeem vouchers on their platforms
                       (e.g., restaurant or food delivery reward redemptions).

      2.      White-Label & API-Based Distribution (B2B / B2B2C): Platforms increasingly operate as gifting
              infrastructure providers, offering technology that partners can brand and distribute as their own. This model is
              best suited for banks, fintechs, large enterprises, and loyalty program operators.

              Revenue Sources
                                                           189
     i.       SaaS Licensing Fees: Licensing APIs, digital wallet software, and gift card management systems to
              banks, fintechs, corporates, and loyalty companies.

     ii.      Setup & Integration Fees: One-time fees for onboarding, customization, and system integration.

     iii.     Platform / Usage Fees: Ongoing charges based on transactions, API calls, or active users.

     Use Cases: Bank-branded reward catalogues, corporate employee reward portals and Fintech cashback &
     incentive engines

3.   Integration into Loyalty, Rewards & Spend Programmes: Digital gift cards function as a reward currency
     embedded within broader customer and employee engagement systems.

     Revenue Sources

     i.       Management Fees: Monthly or annual fees for operating and maintaining loyalty or rewards
              programmes.

     ii.      Reward Redemption Revenue: Variable income linked to the volume or value of rewards redeemed
              by users.

     iii.     Spend-Linked Incentives: Revenue generated through campaigns tied to user spending, milestones, or
              behaviour.

     Common Integrations: Credit card & banking loyalty programmes, FMCG consumer promotions and employee
     recognition & incentive schemes

4.   Subscription & Premium Models: Some platforms layer subscriptions on top of gifting and rewards.

     Revenue Sources

     i.       Premium Memberships: Paid tiers offering enhanced rewards, faster redemptions, or exclusive offers.

     ii.      Enterprise Subscriptions: Annual contracts for advanced analytics, reporting, and program
              customization.

5.   Cashback, Incentives & Funded Promotions–Driven Revenue Model: Cashbacks, instant incentives and
     funded promotional rewards act as a major demand and revenue driver in India’s digital gift card ecosystem.
     Rather than being cost centres, these incentives are typically merchant-funded, brand-sponsored, or co-funded by
     banks and fintechs, creating monetization opportunities for platforms while driving high engagement and
     transaction velocity.

     Revenue Sources

     i.       Merchant-Funded Cashback Campaigns: Brands fund cashback or bonus-value offers on gift cards
              and vouchers to drive customer acquisition, repeat usage, and higher spend. Platforms earn margins or
              campaign fees for designing, hosting, and distributing these offers.

     ii.      Bank & Fintech Incentive Budgets: Banks, wallets, and fintechs allocate marketing and loyalty
              budgets for cashbacks linked to gift card purchases, credit card spends, UPI transactions, or account
              activity. Gifting platforms monetize through campaign fees, distribution commissions, or revenue-
              sharing arrangements.

     iii.     Promotional & Campaign Management Fees: Platforms charge brands and enterprises for end-to-end
              management of incentive campaigns, including offer structuring, targeting, fulfilment, fraud controls,
              and performance analytics.

     iv.      Performance-Linked Revenue: Revenue tied to outcomes such as redemptions, incremental spend,
              repeat transactions, or customer reactivation—aligning platform earnings with campaign success.

     To succeed in India’s digital gift card market, players must balance compliance with innovation, diversify
     partners, invest in fraud prevention and API resilience, and move up the value chain into loyalty, analytics, and
     program management to defend margins. Digital direct-to-consumer ecosystem is powering retail consumption
                                                  190
               through prepaid spends, gifting and rewards.

5.9   Key Risks & Challenges

      India’s digital gift card market operates at the intersection of payments, commerce, and rewards, exposing it to regulatory,
      technological, cultural, and competitive risks, while also competing with fast-growing alternative digital payment options.

      1.       India’s digital gift card market faces a wide set of risks and challenges arising from its overlap with payments,
               commerce, and rewards ecosystems. One of the most significant risks is regulatory & compliance complexity,
               as digital gift cards and wallets often fall under RBI regulations for prepaid payment instruments, along with
               KYC, AML, GST, and data localization requirements.

      2.       Cyber fraud & payment security risks are another major concern. Platforms are vulnerable to phishing,
               unauthorized redemptions, fake or duplicated vouchers, and data breaches involving sensitive customer
               information. These risks erode consumer and enterprise trust, forcing companies to invest heavily in
               cybersecurity, fraud detection, and monitoring systems.

      3.       The market is highly competitive & increasingly saturated, with fintechs, digital wallets, e-commerce
               platforms, banks, loyalty companies, and unorganized players all offering similar gifting solutions. This intense
               competition makes differentiation difficult, while large platforms can bundle gifting into broader ecosystems,
               reducing pricing power for standalone players. At the same time, price-sensitive consumers and enterprise buyers
               negotiate aggressively, leading to margin pressure, especially when combined with payment gateway fees and
               seasonal discounting.

      4.       Consumer adoption of digital gifting in India faces challenges due to a strong cultural preference for cash gifts,
               limited awareness outside metro cities, and concerns over sharing personal/payment data, while friction in
               delivery, redemption, or refunds—along with issues like expiry and unused balances—can reduce user
               satisfaction and impact engagement, especially for enterprise and loyalty programs.

      5.       Operationally, digital gifting platforms face technology, scalability, and integration challenges, including
               ensuring API reliability during peak periods, connecting with legacy bank, HR, and loyalty systems, and
               managing digital inventory, activation delays, reconciliation, and unclaimed balances. Additionally, cash flow
               and working capital pressures arise from pre-funding gift cards, delayed enterprise payments, and highly seasonal
               demand.

6     Multi-Channel Customer Acquisition and Referral-Led Growth Dynamics in Prepaid and Digital Gifting Platforms

      Cashbacks and incentives significantly increase purchase intent, redemption rates, and frequency of use, especially among
      price-sensitive consumers. For corporates and brands, they deliver measurable ROI; for platforms, they act as a scalable
      monetization lever layered across commission, API, and loyalty-based models. In India, cashbacks and incentives are not
      merely promotional tools but structural demand engines that underpin transaction growth, partner monetization, and long-
      term platform stickiness across the digital gifting value chain.

      Companies operating in this domain are increasingly adopting a multi-channel approach to customer acquisition alongside
      their direct-to-consumer strategy. This typically includes a mix of SEO optimization, social media engagement,
      performance marketing, partnerships and collaborations, affiliate programs, as well as referrals, reseller arrangements, and
      on ground activations. These channels work together to drive discovery, engagement, and conversion across different
      consumer touchpoints.

      In addition to acquisition, this multi-channel and referral led approach also supports stronger customer retention by
      enabling continuous engagement across multiple use cases (such as payments, rewards, and gifting), improving stickiness
      of the platform and driving repeat usage; over time, this results in higher organic retention as satisfied users continue to
      transact and also act as advocates, further feeding into referral driven growth loops.

      The cost of acquiring customers (CAC) varies significantly (from ₹ 350 to 550 per user) across these channels depending
      on factors such as product complexity, pricing and margins, scale of operations, and level of competition.

      Within this broader framework, companies are increasingly adopting a referral led growth layer alongside their D2C
      channels. While mobile apps, websites, and digital campaigns enable direct acquisition and engagement, referral networks
      / agents including affiliates, influencers, content platforms, and digital partners help expand reach and accelerate user
      acquisition.

                                                              191
      These referral arrangements are typically structured through performance linked incentive models, where partners are
      compensated based on clearly defined metrics such as new user acquisition (per user referred), transaction throughput (per
      transaction or volume processed), or value-based metrics such as revenue or margin generated from the referred user base;
      this ensures alignment of incentives with business outcomes while enabling scalability of acquisition through partners.
      This is effective in consumer use cases such as prepaid card usage, everyday spend management, rewards redemption, and
      gifting, where discovery and recommendation play a critical role in influencing purchase decisions. Referral partners often
      bring access to high-intent consumer segments, resulting in improved conversion rates and more efficient acquisition.

      While referral incentives are typically paid to ecosystem partners, a portion of these incentives is often indirectly passed
      on to end users through promotional benefits such as cashback, discounts, or bonus rewards, thereby improving customer
      acquisition efficiency and enhancing value perception, while also maintaining partner engagement. Paramotor plans to
      increase the amount they spend on customer acquisition and retention initiatives, such as cashback, user rewards and
      incentives to encourage higher usage of the Prepaid Cards and Gift Cards they distribute, drive issuance and spending
      volumes, and increase overall monetisation per user.

      Across the industry, companies combine D2C ownership of the customer journey with partner-led discovery and
      distribution to scale efficiently. A common approach is to work closely with a select set of high-performing referral
      channels / agents such as influencers, deal platforms, or digital communities and deepen engagement through targeted
      campaigns, personalized offers, and co-branded experiences. This helps drive repeat usage and stronger engagement within
      specific consumer cohorts.

7     Custom Fintech Software Development Market

7.1   Market Overview

      India’s fintech ecosystem is growing rapidly on the back of digital payments, expanding digital identity, and rising
      smartphone / internet penetration. This growth is driving strong demand for custom fintech software across multiple
      segments (cards, vouchers, loyalty, analytics, expense, HR) and across market archetypes (such as issuers, program
      managers, processors, API platforms). Custom software enables banks, fintechs, and enterprises to differentiate their
      products and comply with strict regulations (tokenization, KYC/AML, Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard).

Key Trends

•        Shift Toward API-First and Modular Architectures

         Fintech institutions are increasingly adopting API first and microservices based architectures to enable faster
         integrations and scalability. Custom software is being built in modular components like cards, vouchers, loyalty,
         analytics that can be deployed independently or combined. This approach allows banks, NBFCs, and enterprises
         to plug into payment rails (UPI, card networks), sponsor banks, and third-party ecosystems efficiently.

•        Rise of Embedded Finance Across Sectors

         Non-financial platforms such as e-commerce marketplaces, mobility providers, and SaaS companies are
         embedding financial services into their customer journeys. This is driving demand for custom fintech stacks
         capable of handling card issuance, voucher management, loyalty programs, and payout systems. Embedded
         finance requires deep integration, compliance alignment, and flexible rule engines making custom development
         critical.

•        Cloud-Native and Scalable Infrastructure Adoption

         Cloud infrastructure has become the default deployment model for fintech software. Financial institutions are
         demanding high availability, elastic scaling, containerized environments, and secure cloud-native deployments.
         Custom development now prioritizes resilience, API security, and DevSecOps integration.

•        Growth of Digital Finance Infrastructure for D2C Brands

         Direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands are increasingly adopting embedded financial capabilities as part of their
         customer engagement and revenue strategies. Consumer brands across e-commerce, retail, gaming, and
         subscription services are launching prepaid cards, digital wallets, cashback programs, voucher systems, and
         loyalty-linked financial incentives to deepen customer relationships and improve retention. This shift requires
         flexible fintech infrastructure capable of managing card issuance, reward programs, payout engines, and real-
         time transaction processing while integrating seamlessly with commerce platforms, CRM systems, and customer
         analytics tools. As D2C companies expand globally and operate across multiple payment ecosystems, custom-
         built fintech stacks are becoming critical to manage loyalty economics, promotional spend, and financial
         operations at scale.

•        Increased Regulatory and Compliance Complexity

         RBI mandates around tokenization, PPI frameworks, KYC/AML, and data localization have significantly
         increased system complexity. Organizations require custom built systems that embed compliance natively rather
         than relying on rigid off the shelf platforms. Custom fintech software increasingly incorporates audit trails, risk
         monitoring, and regulatory reporting modules as core features.

•        Growth of Real-Time Analytics & AI-Driven Decisioning

         Financial institutions are moving from static reporting to real time dashboards and predictive analytics. Custom-
         built analytics engines now integrate transaction monitoring, fraud detection, underwriting intelligence, and
         behavioural scoring. AI/ML capabilities are becoming foundational across card systems, loyalty engines, and
         lending modules.

•        Expansion of Corporate Digital Finance Tools

                                                       193
             Corporates are adopting digital expense systems, prepaid card programs, payroll automation, and loyalty-based
             incentive systems. Custom fintech software is increasingly used to integrate financial instruments directly with
             ERP, HRMS, and CRM systems, creating seamless operational workflows.

      Market drivers

      •      Outsourcing of Core Technology Capabilities

             Financial institutions are increasingly outsourcing technology development to specialized fintech software
             providers rather than building large in-house teams. This trend is driven by cost efficiency, speed to market, and
             access to specialized regulatory expertise.

      •      Proliferation of Digital Payments

             India’s massive growth in digital transactions has expanded backend infrastructure needs. India has witnessed a
             sharp acceleration in digital payment adoption over the past decade, driven by coordinated policy initiatives and
             ecosystem development by the Government of India and financial sector stakeholders. The growth of digital
             payments has been supported by widespread adoption of multiple payment rails including BHIM-UPI, debit and
             credit cards, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS), National Electronic Toll Collection
             (NETC), and Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs). These platforms have significantly expanded the scale of
             person-to-person (P2P) and person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions across the country. As transaction volumes
             continue to scale rapidly, financial institutions, fintech companies, and enterprises require robust backend
             infrastructure to support transaction processing, reconciliation, fraud detection, and analytics. This growth is
             consequently driving demand for scalable fintech technology platforms such as card management systems, real-
             time reconciliation dashboards, and advanced fraud monitoring solutions capable of supporting large-scale digital
             payment ecosystems.

      •      Enterprise Digitization and Financial Automation

             Corporates are digitizing expense, payroll, incentive, and loyalty systems to reduce manual processes and increase
             financial transparency. Custom-built fintech tools enable tighter policy control, automated disbursement, and
             real-time reporting across enterprise environments.

      •      Government-Led Digital Infrastructure Push

             India’s digital public infrastructure has significantly reduced friction in identity verification, payments, and data
             sharing. Government initiatives such as Aadhaar for digital identity, Unified Payments Interface (UPI) for real-
             time payments, Account Aggregator Framework for secure financial data sharing, and Open Network for Digital
             Commerce (ONDC) for interoperable digital commerce are accelerating the development of a national digital
             ecosystem. This infrastructure is enabling rapid financial product innovation and increasing demand for custom-
             built integration layers and API-based platforms that allow banks, fintechs, and enterprises to seamlessly connect
             with these national digital rails.

      •      Rising Demand for Differentiated Financial Products

             Banks and fintechs increasingly compete on user experience, loyalty benefits, and flexible financial instruments.
             Custom software enables differentiated card features, voucher logic, reward personalization, and embedded
             financial journeys that generic platforms cannot easily provide.

             These drivers mean banks and fintechs are investing heavily in software yet Indian banks still spend a lower
             fraction of their revenues on technology as compared to their global counterparts, indicating room for new
             vendors. Embedded finance is rising (fintech APIs for commerce / loans), and sectors like BNPL, MSME lending
             are on upticks. Overall, custom fintech software development is part of a fast-growing vertical within India’s
             overall fintech-SaaS market, projected to grow to 4X its size in 2025 by 2030.

             The market is complex, with a broad stakeholder ecosystem (issuers, sponsor banks, card networks, merchants,
             regulators, fintech SaaS vendors). Custom software vendors must navigate compliance certifications,
             partnerships, and challenging sales cycles. Recommended strategies include focusing on high-criticality
             segments, partnering with banks/networks early, building modular API-based platforms, and aligning pricing to
             performance.

7.2   Scope of Custom Fintech Software Development
                                                            194
•   Card Management Systems (CMS): Custom CMS handle card issuance and lifecycle for issuers (banks,
    fintech lenders, corporates). Typical buyers are banks/ PPI issuer rolling out payment cards. The value proposition
    is fully controlling card parameters (BIN management, EMV setup, tokenization per RBI guidelines, integration
    to networks/PGs). Custom CMS is critical. Without it, banks cannot issue or manage cards reliably.

•   Voucher / Gift Card Management Systems: This segment covers electronic gift card and voucher issuance,
    management, and redemption platforms used by retailers, malls, e-commerce companies, and corporate incentive
    programs. Typical buyers include retailers, e-commerce marketplaces, corporates running employee or channel
    incentive programs, and fintech companies offering gift-based Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs). These
    platforms enable businesses to issue digital vouchers, manage redemption workflows, and track usage across
    multiple channels. Custom software typically manages voucher generation, code lifecycle management, reload
    limits, expiration rules, merchant acceptance configurations, and regulatory constraints. It also integrates with
    payment networks, merchant POS systems, and e-commerce platforms to support seamless omnichannel
    redemption. In India, the market for voucher and gift card management platforms is relatively specialized with a
    limited number of technology providers offering scalable infrastructure and network integrations. Prominent
    players operating in this space include Paramotor, Pine Labs Ltd., Vouchagram India Pvt. Ltd., and other voucher
    network operators that enable large-scale issuance and redemption ecosystems for retailers and corporate clients.
    A robust voucher management system is critical for retail loyalty and corporate gifting programs, as it helps
    prevent fraud, ensures compliance with regulatory requirements such as KYC for high-value vouchers, and
    supports secure and scalable digital distribution across both online and offline merchant networks.

•   Loyalty Management Systems (LMS): These handle rewards / points programs for customers. Buyers
    include banks, airlines / hotels, large retailers and payment firms. Custom LMS track earn/spend rules,
    membership tiers, partner catalogues, and omnichannel redemption. They integrate with CRM and payment
    systems. The system is critical for loyalty-heavy businesses, as software enables personalized rewards and
    customer engagement.

•   Reporting & Analytics Dashboards: Real-time transaction monitoring, reconciliation and risk
    analytics platforms. Buyers include banks, fintechs (issuers, wallets, NBFCs), and large merchants / corporates.
    This custom software ingests payment / transaction data to provide dashboards for finance teams and compliance
    officers. It often includes AML/KYC monitoring, fraud alerts, reconciliation of clearing/settlement, and spend
    analytics. These systems are critical, since regulators require reporting and firms need real-time insight to detect
    anomalies. The value is operational efficiency and compliance, e.g. 24×7 dashboard on transaction volume spikes,
    automated reconciliation across schemes, drilldowns of anomalous payments.

•   Expense Management Systems: Software for corporate expense control and employee spend. Buyers are
    enterprises and SMBs (especially those issuing corporate cards or travel cards). The system covers policy
    definitions, multi-level approvals, integration with corporate cards, and ERP. The value is automating and
    enforcing spend policies (e.g. daily limits, category controls). The system is important for finance teams, but
    companies sometimes use off-the-shelf solutions. A custom solution is needed when integration with company-
    specific workflows or fintech-issued expense cards is required.

•   Expense Management Systems for Users (D2C Spend Management): This segment covers consumer-facing
    spend management platforms embedded within fintech applications such as Paramotor Digital Technology’s
    SpendPro. These systems allow individual users to track, categorize, and control their spending across cards,
    wallets, and digital payment instruments. Typical buyers include fintech companies, neobanks, digital wallets,
    consumer platforms, and D2C brands offering financial services to their user base. The software enables features
    such as transaction categorization, real-time spending insights, budgeting tools, merchant-level analytics, reward
    tracking, and card controls (e.g., spend limits, category blocking, location-based controls). It integrates directly
    with payment rails, card management systems, and loyalty platforms to provide a unified financial dashboard for
    users. As digital payments grow and consumers increasingly use multiple financial instruments, spend
    management tools are becoming a key differentiator for fintech platforms. These systems enhance customer
    engagement, enable behavioural insights, and support financial wellness features such as budgeting alerts and
    personalized reward optimization. Custom-built platforms offer deeper analytics, integration with loyalty
    programs and financial products, and the ability to scale across large consumer bases.

•   HR / Payroll Systems (Fintech-enabled): Encompasses employee payroll disbursement and benefits via fintech
    rails. Buyers are mid-large enterprises and banks offering payroll accounts to corporates. Custom software
    automates salary payments, tax/benefit calculations, and integration with attendance systems. It includes features
    like bulk payouts and real-time salary disbursement on paydays. Traditional HR systems suffice for many, but
    fintech-enabled payroll is growing. A custom fintech HR system adds value by improving cashflow and by
                                                  195
               enabling differential disbursements.

7.3   Role of Customized Software Development

      Custom fintech software sits across the value-chain archetypes: program managers (e.g. loyalty or voucher program
      aggregators), issuers (banks/PPI issuers issuing cards and wallets), card processors, BaaS/B2B platforms, and API players.
      For example, a bank may commission a custom CMS and analytics suite; a retailer may need a bespoke voucher and
      loyalty platform; a third-party service provider may act as a processor and deploy a tokenization engine for its partners. In
      each case, custom software provides differentiation and tight integration with existing systems. Service such as DevStack
      by Paramotor Digital Technology Ltd. illustrate how modular custom development frameworks are increasingly being
      used to build fintech applications spanning rewards infrastructure, spend management systems, embedded payments, and
      enterprise-grade digital workflows. Off the shelf solutions often lack deep integration (e.g. specific regulatory compliance),
      so custom development is critical to implement complex flows.

      Business Models for Fintech Software Providers

      Vendors typically use a mix of revenue models:

      •        Software Licensing / SaaS: Monthly / annual fees for platform access; very common for cloud-deployed
               solutions.

      •        Usage or API Fees: Pay per transaction or per API call pricing (e.g. for payment gateway or tokenization API
               usage).

      •        Implementation Services: Upfront fees for customization, integrations and deployment.

      •        Revenue Sharing: In some partnerships (e.g., with lenders or BNPL startups), a share of interest or interchange
               fees.

      •        Managed Services: Ongoing operations support contracts (helpdesk, maintenance).

      Many vendors bundle models (e.g. low subscription + per-user or per-transaction charges), or offer platform + integration
      packages for large clients.

8     Bill Payments Platform Market

      The Indian bill payments platform market is increasingly centred on the BBPS, which acts as the interoperable national
      backbone for recurring bill payments across categories such as electricity, gas, water, telecom, DTH, FASTag, loan
      repayment, insurance, municipal taxes, and more recently credit card bills. Bharat Connect is India’s unified bill payment
      platform which is operated by NPCI Bharat BillPay Limited and is backed by the Reserve Bank of India, ensuring secure
      and accessible transactions through various digital and physical channels.

      In practical terms, this market includes consumer-facing bill payment applications, merchant and assisted-payment
      interfaces, biller integrations, Biller Operating Units (BOUs) (licensed entities, often banks, that can onboard billers into
      the BBPS ecosystem acting as critical regulated interfaces between billers and the central network), technology platforms,
      APIs, and orchestration layers that connect billers, banks, payment apps, and settlement systems. This is precisely the
      operating context relevant to offerings such as Paramotor Digital Technology Ltd.’s Bharat Connect bill payment platform.

payment category but have evolved into a broader digital payments infrastructure layer that is deepening across household
finance, mobility, credit, and assisted commerce.

One of the most important recent shifts has been the inclusion of credit card bill payments into the Bharat Connect
ecosystem. The share of credit card bill payments in Bharat Connect transaction value had risen sharply, supported by the
RBI-driven transition requiring such payments through the BBPS framework for third-party app flows. This has
significantly expanded the addressable transaction value of the ecosystem and has moved the platform beyond traditional
utility collections into higher-value recurring payments.

Another notable trend is the increasing diversification of usage channels. Bill payments are no longer confined to direct
bank channels or standalone utility apps. They are increasingly being facilitated through consumer payment apps, merchant
ecosystems, assisted commerce networks, API platforms, and embedded fintech journeys. Market reporting shows major
consumer apps participating in the ecosystem, while assisted networks are scaling bill-pay usage in rural and semi-urban
India. This channel diversification is increasing the strategic importance of platforms that can enable interoperable, secure,
multi-channel bill payment journeys.

The market is also becoming increasingly API-driven and infrastructure-led. Platforms, for example, explicitly position
themselves as a BBPS integration bridge between billers and BOU banks, simplifying onboarding, integrations, reporting,
notifications, and settlements. This is an important signal that the bill payments market is not only a consumer payments
market, but also a platform infrastructure market, where the ability to abstract compliance, routing, reconciliation, and
integration complexity creates significant enterprise value.

      The strongest macro driver behind the bill payments platform market is the structural formalization and digitization of
      recurring payments in India. Recurring payments such as electricity, telecom, insurance, FASTag, and loan EMI
      collections represent frequent, high-volume, non-discretionary transactions. As more of these flows move into
      interoperable digital infrastructure, platforms that enable bill presentment, authentication, payment routing, confirmation,
      and reconciliation become increasingly essential. Bharat Connect was created precisely to digitize and standardize this
      layer of the economy.

      A second major demand driver is regulatory standardization. The integration of recurring bill payments under the
      BBPS/Bharat Connect framework improves transaction certainty, interoperability, and auditability. The RBI-linked
      transition of credit card bill payments into this framework has materially expanded the ecosystem and also demonstrated
      the policy direction: more bill-like and recurring payment flows are likely to be standardized under common rails over
      time. This supports long-term demand for compliant bill payment infrastructure, biller onboarding layers, and platform
      orchestration capabilities.

      A third key driver is the rise of consumer super-apps and fintech-led payment engagement. Bill payments are strategically
      attractive because they drive repeat app usage, customer retention, and wallet share. As more apps attempt to retain users
      across multiple financial activities, bill pay becomes an anchor use case.

      Fourth, merchant and assisted-commerce expansion is widening the addressable market. Rural and semi-urban consumers,
      small merchants, and assisted digital finance agents increasingly use interoperable bill payment infrastructure. Bill pay
      platforms are not merely urban, app-based propositions; they are also becoming part of India’s broader assisted digital
      commerce infrastructure.

      Fifth, enterprises and billers themselves are increasingly seeking simplified connectivity to BBPS rails. The more
      categories that get added, the greater the complexity in onboarding, settlement handling, notifications, reporting, exception
      management, and BOU coordination. This is why technology providers have found market traction with API-led offerings
      that reduce time to integration and compliance complexity. Paramotor Digital Technology Ltd.’s own positioning as an
      all-in-one multi-mode bill payment platform reflects the same underlying demand for simplified and unified bill payment
      experiences.

8.2   Value Chain and Stakeholder Ecosystem

      The bill payments platform market in India operates through a layered ecosystem.

      At the top sits NPCI Bharat BillPay / Bharat Connect, which provides the interoperable switching, rules, standards, and
      central framework for bill payments. It defines operating requirements and enables standardization across the ecosystem.

      The next layer consists of Biller Operating Units (BOUs) and banks. BOUs are licensed entities, often banks, that can
      onboard billers into the BBPS ecosystem. They act as critical regulated interfaces between billers and the central network.

      The third layer consists of billers like utilities, telecom operators, FASTag issuers, insurers, lenders, municipal bodies, and
      card issuers that generate bills and seek digital collections through interoperable rails. As more categories move onto
      Bharat Connect, the diversity and strategic importance of this biller layer increase. Credit card issuers joining the network
      have already materially expanded transaction values.


                                                               198
      The fourth layer comprises platform enablers and APIs, which is where companies like Paramotor and potentially
      DevStack like custom platform providers fit. This layer handles biller onboarding workflows, API integrations, compliance
      abstraction, reporting, settlement workflows, alerts, dashboards, and enterprise-grade routing capability. This layer is
      strategically valuable because it simplifies complexity for billers, fintechs, and merchants.

      The fifth layer includes consumer apps, payment apps, merchant interfaces, and assisted commerce channels. These are
      the visible channels through which users make bill payments. Examples include bank apps, consumer payment apps, credit
      card repayment apps, merchant-led collections interfaces, and assisted commerce platforms. High-volume consumer apps
      derive engagement and retention benefits from embedding bill-pay capabilities.

      The final layer is the end user, including consumers, merchants, and assisted-commerce customers. Their needs are centred
      around convenience, reliability, instant confirmation, payment choice, and trust. Paramotor Digital Technology Ltd.’s own
      product messaging ‘unified bill payments, instant confirmation, secure multi-mode transactions’ maps directly to these
      user expectations.

      Taken together, the ecosystem involves at least six strategic stakeholder groups: NPCI Bharat BillPay, regulator-linked
      infrastructure, BOUs/banks, billers, technology/API enablers, and front-end distribution channels. Platforms that can
      connect these layers efficiently, compliantly, and at scale occupy a high-value position in the market.

8.3   Key Risks & Challenges

      The bill payments platform market faces some structural risks. First, the ecosystem is highly dependent on the
      BBPS/Bharat Connect regulatory framework, making participants vulnerable to policy changes, onboarding rules, and
      integration standards that can quickly reshape market dynamics.

      Second, front-end distribution power is concentrated among a few large payment apps, which control user traffic and may
      exert pricing pressure on mid-stack infrastructure providers.

      Third, the market involves significant technology and integration complexity, including bill fetching, authentication,
      settlement, notifications, and dispute handling across thousands of billers.

      Fourth, unit economics can be challenging, as bill payments are often used to drive engagement and retention rather than
      as a standalone high-margin revenue stream.

      Finally, competition is intensifying from fintech infrastructure providers, payment apps, and commerce platforms
      embedding bill payments into broader financial workflows.

      However, for technology vendors, the bill payments platform market is attractive because it combines high transaction
      recurrence, regulatory formalization, deep integration needs, and channel diversification. However, value creation is likely
      to be strongest not at the commoditized front-end alone, but in the compliance, orchestration, API, integration, and
      enterprise enablement layers of the stack. That is where complexity is highest, switching costs can deepen over time, and
      platform providers can create differentiated value.

      acceptance and access to network-specific offers. Its platforms support digital issuance, spend management, rewards
      redemption, configurable loyalty programs and other fintech solutions for consumers and enterprises.

      Paramotor’s revenue profile is increasingly diversifying beyond program fee income toward rewards and loyalty solutions

      focused model toward a broader embedded fintech and digital engagement platform ecosystem. Through RewardOn,

      Pine Labs Limited (‘Pine Labs’) is a merchant commerce, digital payments, and financial technology platform company
      focused on enabling end-to-end commerce and payment solutions for merchants, enterprises, financial institutions, and
      consumers. The company provides integrated payment acceptance infrastructure across online and offline channels,
      including point-of-sale (“POS”) terminals, QR-based payments, payment gateways, merchant acquiring enablement, and
      omnichannel commerce solutions. In addition to payment acceptance, Pine Labs offers prepaid and gift card issuance and
      processing solutions, loyalty and rewards management platforms, buy-now-pay-later (“BNPL”) and EMI solutions,
      invoice financing, and merchant-focused embedded financial services. The company also supports enterprise gifting,
      customer engagement, and prepaid commerce programs for brands and corporates. Pine Labs operates through partnerships
      with banks, card networks, merchants, brands, and fintech ecosystem participants, enabling digital transaction processing,
      merchant engagement, and consumer financing capabilities across retail, e-commerce, hospitality, and enterprise sectors.
      Its platforms are designed to support seamless commerce enablement, transaction management, customer acquisition, and
      merchant monetization across a large and diversified merchant ecosystem.

      Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services Limited (‘Zaggle’) is a financial technology and SaaS-based spend management
      company focused on corporate payments, prepaid card solutions, employee expense management, rewards and incentives,
      and enterprise financial workflow automation. The company provides integrated platforms that enable businesses to
      manage employee reimbursements, corporate spends, channel partner incentives, vendor payouts, employee benefits, and
      customer engagement programs through digital payment and prepaid instrument solutions. Zaggle partners with banks and
      payment network providers to issue prepaid cards, forex cards, meal benefit cards, and corporate payment instruments
      while also offering software-based expense management and spend analytics solutions. Its product portfolio includes
      corporate spend management platforms, rewards and recognition solutions, tax-benefit employee programs, invoice and
      vendor payment management systems, and workflow automation tools for enterprises. The company serves clients across
      sectors such as banking and financial services, technology, healthcare, manufacturing, retail, and consumer industries.
      Zaggle’s integrated fintech and SaaS ecosystem combines payment infrastructure, analytics, automation, and compliance
      management capabilities to help enterprises optimize operational efficiency, improve spend visibility, and enhance
      employee and customer engagement.

      Capillary Technologies India Limited (‘Capillary’) is a customer engagement, loyalty management, and AI-driven
      marketing technology company focused on enabling enterprises to strengthen customer retention, personalization, and
      omnichannel consumer engagement. The company provides cloud-based software platforms and solutions including
      loyalty program management, customer data platforms (“CDP”), campaign orchestration, rewards management, customer
      analytics, and AI-enabled marketing automation tools. Its platforms leverage artificial intelligence, machine learning,
      predictive analytics, and consumer behaviour insights to help enterprises manage customer lifecycle engagement, targeted
      promotions, personalization strategies, and rewards ecosystems across digital and offline channels. Capillary serves
      retailers, brands, quick-service restaurants, consumer goods companies, fashion and lifestyle brands, and other enterprises
      seeking to improve customer acquisition, retention, and repeat purchase behaviour. The company’s solutions support
      enterprises in integrating customer data across multiple touchpoints, enabling real-time engagement, loyalty-led
      commerce, targeted marketing campaigns, and data-driven decision-making. In addition, Capillary offers analytics and
      engagement capabilities focused on improving customer lifetime value, strengthening brand affinity, and driving repeat
      transactions within enterprise loyalty and rewards ecosystems.

      Pine Labs, Zaggle and Capillary are hereby collectively considered as the listed peer set (‘listed peers’).

Notes for Paramotor Digital Technology Limited :
(1) Revenue from operations for the period/year as appearing in the Statement of Profit and Loss in the Restated Financial Information
(2) EBITDA is an acronym for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation, which has been calculated by adding (i) finance costs, (ii) total tax
        expenses and (iii) depreciation and amortisation expense, and subtracting other income from profit after tax from continuing operations for the period/year
        (“EBITDA”).
(3) EBITDA Margin is EBITDA expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations (“EBITDA Margin”).
(4) Profit after tax for the period/year from continuing operations as appearing in the Statement of profit and Loss in the Restated Financial Information.
(5) PAT Margin is profit after tax for the period/year from continuing operations expressed as a percentage of revenue from operations (“PAT Margin”).
(6) Current Ratio is calculated as total current assets divided by total current liabilities.
(7) Net Capital Turnover Ratio is calculated as revenue from operations (from continuing operations) divided by Working Capital. Working Capital is calculated
        as current assets minus current liabilities (“Working Capital”).
(8) Return on equity (RoE) is calculated as Profit/(loss) for the period/year from continuing operations divided by Average Total Equity. Average Total Equity is
        calculated as total equity as at the beginning of the period/year plus total equity as at the end of the period/year, divided by two (“Average Total Equity”).
(9) Revenue from operations by type of income
        •   Reward points business refers to revenue from company’s Rewards & loyalty business. This revenue is recognised on a gross basis.
        •   Program Fees refers to revenue from company’s PPI Program Management and Distribution business. This revenue is recognised on a net basis.
        •   Platform Fee/Service Fee refers to revenue from providing technical and platform development services to businesses, which the company has branded
             as “DevStack”. This revenue is recognised on a gross basis.
(10) User Retention Rate refers to the percentage of transacting users in a given year who had also transacted in the immediately preceding year. This metric is
        only evaluated on an annual basis.
(11) Total transacting Users refers to the number of users who have completed at least one transaction within the period/year
(12) The average revenue per transacting user is calculated as revenue from operations divided by total transacting users. Company believes the total revenue
        from operations to be a more meaningful metric than average revenue per transacting user as the Revenue from their Rewards and Loyalty Business and
        DevStack is recognised on a gross basis while Program Fee revenue is recognised on a net basis in accordance with Ind AS 115, and a single user journey
        may simultaneously generate both gross and net inflows across business verticals, making per-user metrics less meaningful in their view. Further, under the
        RBI regulatory framework governing Prepaid Payment Instruments, they receive only a consolidated share of interchange from PPI issuers and do not have
        access to card-level or user-level spend data.
(13) User acquisition and retention expenses for the period/year as appearing in the Statement of Profit and Loss in the Restated Financial Information. Amounts
        include certain amounts paid to certain related parties for referral and distribution services and Company confirms that all such payments were made on an
        arms’ length basis and no portion of the Net Proceeds are proposed to be paid to such related parties
(14) User acquisition and retention expenses as a percentage of revenue from operations refers to User acquisition and retention expenses divided by revenue from
        operations
(15) The Average user acquisition and retention expenses per transacting user refers to total user acquisition and retention expenses divided by total transacting
        users. Company believes that the user acquisition and retention expenses as a percentage of revenue from operations is a more meaningful metric than average
        user acquisition and retention expenses per transacting user as the User acquisition and retention expenses may be incurred at an

                                                                                  208
    offering/platform/distribution-channel level and may not be attributable to specific users, and expenditure incurred in a period may result to users acquired
    or retained in a different period.



Paramotor Digital Technology Limited’s business model is characterized by diversified revenue streams across consumer-led use
cases spanning spend, rewards, digital gifting and fintech solutions, enabling multiple monetization levers and reducing dependence
on any single product or segment. By combining its consumer-facing and enterprise offerings across SpendPro, RewardOn,
yayyy.shop and DevStack with a scalable technology platform, diversified monetization model and partnership-led growth strategy,
supported by an experienced management team, the company is positioned to power the modern consumer ecosystem and capture
opportunities across the evolving digital commerce, engagement and payments ecosystem. Paramotor Digital Technology Limited
has demonstrated significant user scale expansion, with total transacting users increasing from 7,869 in Fiscal Year 2023 to over
1.5 million users in Fiscal Year 2026, supported by the scaling of its offerings across consumer spend, digital gifting, rewards and
loyalty, and fintech solutions.
Paramotor Digital Technology Limited has achieved strong financial performance relative to its selected peers, characterized by
growth, profitability, and efficient capital utilization. In Fiscal 2026, Paramotor had the highest Profit After Tax Margin compared
to their listed peers.

OVERVIEW

We are a financial technology company focused on digital gifting, consumer spend management, and rewards and loyalty
platforms. Our platforms comprise yayyy.shop (our direct-to-consumer (“D2C”) digital marketplace), SpendPro (a D2C spend
management platform), and RewardOn (our business-to-business-to-consumer (“B2B2C”) rewards and loyalty platform),
through which we have served 634,316 and 1,575,830 transacting users in India for the three months period ended June 30,
2026 and Fiscal 2026, respectively. We also offer technical and platform development services to businesses, which we have
branded as “DevStack” (business-to-business (“B2B”)).

We act as a program manager, business correspondent and distribution agent for non-reloadable prepaid payment instruments
(“PPIs”) with a maximum value of ₹10,000 issued by banks and RBI licensed issuers (which we refer to as “PPI Issuers” and
such cards, “Prepaid Cards”) and act as a distribution agent for non-reloadable brand gift cards (PPIs) issued by merchants
(which we refer to as “Gift Cards”). We refer to these activities as our “PPI Program Management and Distribution”
                                                                  210
business. We offer consumer spend management through our SpendPro platform to our users of the Prepaid Cards.

Our Rewards and Loyalty business comprises: (i) reward points and our own reward points card, the “yayyy Reward Points
Card”, which can be purchased directly through our digital marketplace on the yayyy.shop website and mobile application and
used to redeem Gift Cards and Prepaid Cards available on our marketplace; and (ii) our RewardOn platform, a comprehensive,
end-to-end digital rewards and incentives platform that enables corporate customers to design, manage, and distribute reward
points to user beneficiaries which can be redeemed digitally through a configurable rules engine integrated with a customised
catalogue of Gift Cards, Prepaid Cards and the yayyy Reward Points Card. We refer to these activities as our “Rewards and
Loyalty” business. The Rewards and Loyalty business was launched on August 1, 2025.

  PPI Program Management and Distribution business

a) Prepaid Cards

  India’s Prepaid Cards market has been experiencing accelerated growth, primarily driven by the cards’ multifaceted utility of
  both reloadable and non-reloadable prepaid instruments that seamlessly fits into diverse aspects of daily financial life and
  business operations (source: F&S Report, page 16). These cards offer secure, convenient, and pre-funded solutions, appealing
  to both urban consumers and digitally transitioning users (source: F&S Report, page 16).

  As at June 30, 2026, we acted as a (i) program manager for six PPI Issuers, including NSDL Payments Bank Limited, and (ii)
  the distribution agent for two program managers of Prepaid Cards. We refer to the PPI Issuers for whom we act as a program
  manager and the program managers for whom we act as a distribution agent as our “PPI Partners”. These partnerships enable
  us to distribute Prepaid Cards issued across three prominent payment networks, including Visa, RuPay and Mastercard,
  ensuring broad merchant acceptance and access to network-specific offers (source: F&S Report, page 54).




  We offer Prepaid Cards through the following channels: (1) our yayyy.shop website and a mobile application, (available on
  well-known application marketplaces), (2) our sales operations team, and (3) our ecosystem partners who act as referral agents
  and distribution partners (“Ecosystem Partners”). A user can opt for delivery of a physical card or virtual card through an
  instant messaging application or email.

  We earn revenue from acting as a program manager, business correspondent and distribution agent for Prepaid Cards from our
  share of interchange fees generated on spends on Prepaid Cards at merchant outlets (at physical stores and online), comprising
  (i) our agreed share of the interchange fees with the PPI Partners, including NSDL Payments Bank Limited, and (ii) income
  from a third-party service that provide transaction switching services to banks in the form of incentives to promote issuer
  specific programs. We entered into a co-brand agreement with Mastercard Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd. in March 2026 for Prepaid
  Cards co-branded with us. These Prepaid Cards will be issued by one or more of our PPI Partners. We are entitled to receive
  incentive based income in consideration for the promotion of network-specific programmes for Prepaid Cards from a network
  provider.

  In furtherance of our agreement with NSDL Payments Bank Limited in December 2025 to distribute mono-branded Prepaid
  Cards, in July 2026 we entered into a co-brand agreement with NSDL Payments Bank Limited for Prepaid Cards. Additionally,
  in June 2026, we entered into an agreement with a new PPI Issuer to market and distribute their PPIs.

                                                                    212
  Users of the Prepaid Cards issued by our PPI Partners can use our SpendPro platform, which serves as the spend management
  platform, enabling users to access virtual cards, track real-time transaction feeds, receive real-time alerts, manage stored-
  value limits, allowing users to monitor spends and check applicable spending limits, and instant card controls, such as, instant
  freeze of the card. We currently do not charge fees for using SpendPro.




b) Gift Cards

  We distribute Gift Cards which are non-reloadable brand gift cards issued by merchants, to users through our yayyy.shop
  website and a mobile application, (available on well-known application marketplaces), which were launched in second and
  fourth quarters of Fiscal 2026, respectively. Our yayyy.shop website and mobile application support the prompt digital delivery
  of Gift Cards through instant messaging and email, providing a streamlined gifting experience. These Gift Cards are not
  reloadable. These Gift Cards can be spent offline at the respective brand’s physical stores or online through the brand’s website
  or application (where applicable).




  As at June 30, 2026, we act as a distribution agent for Gift Cards for three aggregators of Gift Cards (“Gift Card Aggregators”).
                                                                  213
As at June 30, 2026, we offered a catalogue of 234 Gift Cards covering national and international brands across fashion,
electronics, dining, travel, and e-commerce platforms. We earn commission income from Gift Card Aggregators for facilitating
the distribution of Gift Cards to users.




Rewards and Loyalty Business

Our Rewards and Loyalty business comprises: (i) reward points and our own reward points card, the “yayyy Reward Points
Card”, which can be purchased directly through our digital marketplace on the yayyy.shop website and mobile application and
used to redeem Gift Cards and Prepaid Cards available on our marketplace; and (ii) our RewardOn platform, a comprehensive,
end-to-end digital rewards and incentives platform that enables corporate customers to design, manage, and distribute reward
points to end-user beneficiaries, which can be redeemed digitally through a configurable rules engine integrated with a
customised catalogue of Gift Cards, Prepaid Cards and the yayyy Reward Points Card.




Users can purchase reward points or our own reward points card, the “yayyy Reward Points Card”, directly through our digital
marketplace on the yayyy.shop website and mobile application (available on a well-known application marketplace). The
reward points can be used to redeem Gift Cards and Prepaid Cards available on our marketplace. The yayyy Reward Points
Card provides users with enhanced flexibility regarding both the timing and method by which they may access their rewards.
Our yayyy Reward Points Card is particularly suitable for those who wish to give a gift but leave the choice of which Gift
                                                              214
Card(s) to give to the recipient. Our yayyy.shop website and mobile application support the prompt digital delivery of Gift
Cards and Prepaid Cards through instant messaging and email, providing a streamlined gifting experience. As at June 30, 2026,
we offered a catalogue of 234 Gift Cards on yayyy.shop covering national and international brands across fashion, electronics,
dining, travel, and e-commerce platforms.

Our RewardOn platform, which was launched in the second quarter of Fiscal 2026, is a comprehensive, end-to-end digital
rewards and incentives platform that enables corporate customers to design, administer, and deliver structured reward,
recognition, and engagement programs for employees, channel partners, distributors or other beneficiaries. RewardOn provides
corporate customers with the flexibility to tailor reward programs to their specific objectives. We had six and five corporate
customers using the RewardOn platform for the three months period ended June 30, 2026 and Fiscal 2026, respectively.
Through the RewardOn platform, reward points are purchased by the corporate customers and are allocated to users
(beneficiaries), who redeem reward points for Gift Cards across categories, such as fashion, electronics, dining, travel, and e-
commerce platforms through a catalogue available and Prepaid Cards (if applicable) for each rewards and loyalty program.
Corporate customers can curate and select specific Gift Cards they want to make available for redemption from the entire
catalogue of Gift Cards available, which also includes yayyy Reward Points Card, which can be redeemed only on our
yayyy.shop website. As at June 30, 2026, we offered Prepaid Cards and a catalogue of 234 Gift Cards, covering national and
international brands across fashion, electronics, dining, travel, and e-commerce platforms on the RewardOn platform, which
were sourced from three Gift Card Aggregators and three dealers of Gift Cards (“Gift Card Dealers”), who procure Gift Cards
from Gift Card Aggregators and/or other gift card distributors for onward distribution. We are responsible for end-to-end
program management, including configuration and administration, the provisioning of Gift Cards, yayyy Reward Points Cards
and Prepaid Cards, maintenance of technology infrastructure, creating management reports, user support and grievance
redressal.




We also offer our RewardOn platform as a white-label solution for companies to run their own loyalty and rewards programs,
which forms part of our DevStack business.

DevStack

DevStack, launched in the first quarter of Fiscal 2026, is our technical and platform development services designed for the
creation of customised enterprise software applications. Built on the technology infrastructure that powers our other platforms,
RewardOn, and yayyy.shop, DevStack enables clients to leverage market-tested, production-ready components, reducing the
time and effort of undertaking ground up development and lowering implementation risk.

The DevStack platform provides a comprehensive Application Programming Interface (“API”) and Software Development
Kit (“SDK”) layer that enables integration of core functionalities, including KYC onboarding, card management system and
wallets as per different use cases. It additionally offers configurable workflows and customisable user interface components
that integrate directly with users’ existing mobile and web experiences, reducing development complexity and implementation
                                                                215
delays attributed to undertaking ground up development.

The underlying architecture supports multiple tenants through a central “tenant-as-a-service” framework, enabling distinct
brands and partners to operate on shared infrastructure, while maintaining independent configurations, branding, and user
management (source: F&S Report, page 54). This technology led approach supports efficient scaling of transaction volumes
while maintaining reliability, security, and compliance (source: F&S Report, page 54).

Beyond its core technical offerings, DevStack supports platform development, and technical build services, including tailored
ready-to-deploy solutions built on our architecture that can be adapted and white-labelled to meet the specific requirements of
customers.

We generate revenue from DevStack through Platform Fee/Service Fee for our technical development services offered through
DevStack.




Our platforms are built as secure, API-driven infrastructure, designed for reliability. We operate an ecosystem-driven model
built on integrations with external stakeholders, including PPI Partners, Gift Card Aggregators and Gift Card Dealers. These
integrations enable incorporation of third-party offerings into our platforms and solutions. Our three core platforms, SpendPro,
RewardOn, and yayyy.shop, are integrated with relevant third-party systems for issuance, redemption, and settlement, enabling
real-time synchronisation and automation across the value chain. By leveraging reusable service blocks and integrations, our
technology framework enables configurability, interoperability, and rapid deployment across use cases.

OUR STRENGTHS

    1. Digital direct to consumer ecosystem powering retail consumption through prepaid cards, gifting and rewards

We operate digital direct to consumer platforms spanning consumer spend management, rewards and loyalty, and gifting. We
facilitate consumer spending across retail merchants’ physical stores and e-commerce platforms by positioning Prepaid and
Gift Cards as a practical alternative for everyday retail consumption.

Digital payment transactions in India have risen from 21 billion transactions in Fiscal Year 2017-2018 to a substantial 187
billion transactions in Fiscal Year 2023-2024 and 228 billion in Fiscal Year 2024-2025, growing at a CAGR of 40.6 per cent
from Fiscal Year 2018 to Fiscal Year 2025 (source: F&S Report, page 21). This growth has become a defining feature of the
country’s economic landscape, driven by a confluence of factors (source: F&S Report, page 12). Government-led initiatives
such as Digital India have built robust digital infrastructure, expanding access across urban and rural areas (source: F&S
Report, page 12). Digital payments acceptance infrastructure in India has expanded significantly, with the number of point-of-
sale (PoS) terminals standing at over 11 million as at December 31, 2025 (source: F&S Report, page 12).

Prepaid cards, including reloadable and non-reloadable variants, have become integral to modern consumer behaviour, with
total prepaid transactions in India estimated to reach 2.0 billion in Calendar Year 2025 and ₹700.9 billion in terms of transaction
value reflecting broad adoption across categories such as retail, travel, and everyday purchases (source: F&S Report, page 16).
Growth is expected to remain consistent over the next five years, with total prepaid transactions in India projected to reach 4.5
billion and ₹1,028.9 billion in value by Calendar Year 2030, reflecting strong acceptance of the prepaid card model (source: F&S
Report, page 16). From Calendar Year 2025 to Calendar Year 2030, India’s digital gift card market is projected to grow at a
robust CAGR of 17.4%, reaching USD 33.65 billion by Calendar Year 2030 (source: F&S Report, page 22). This rapid
expansion is supported by the convenience and flexibility of digital gift cards, wider corporate adoption for employee rewards
and client engagement, increasing personalization, e-commerce penetration, and sustained festive demand. Spend
management platforms can integrate these incentives into payment flows, allowing consumers to combine budgeting with
promotional benefits such as cashback or merchant discounts (source: F&S Report, page 22).

Digital and e-gift cards continue to gain traction as the preferred gifting instrument due to their convenience, instant delivery,
and flexibility (source: F&S Report, page 40). They are increasingly replacing physical gift options, appealing to both
consumers and corporates looking for hassle-free gifting solutions (source: F&S Report, page 40). The seamless integration of
digital gifting with mobile wallets, UPI, and fintech apps has made purchasing, sending, and redeeming digital gifts faster,
secure, and frictionless (source: F&S Report, page 40). Furthermore, businesses are increasingly incorporating digital gifting
into employee rewards, channel incentives, and customer engagement programs (source: F&S Report, page 40). In India, the
B2B segment represents a major share of gift card usage, with corporate entities increasingly adopting digital gift cards for
rewards, incentives, and promotional campaigns (source: F&S Report, page 40). Adoption continues to grow across sectors
such as IT, retail, financial services, and consumer goods, as companies rely on digital gift cards as a preferred tool for
engagement, motivation, and retention (source: F&S Report, page 40).

As at June 30, 2026, we acted as a (a) program manager for six PPI Issuers, and (b) the distribution agent for two program
managers of Prepaid Cards.

SpendPro, our spend management platform, enables users to track, manage, and analyse spending on Prepaid Cards. SpendPro
provides consumers with spending controls, real-time transaction alerts, and card freeze controls, while stored-value limits
mitigate exposure to unauthorised transactions by capping liability at the available prepaid balance.

We act as distribution agent for Gift Card distributor for three Gift Card Aggregators as at June 30, 2026, offering access to
234 Gift Cards, with prompt digital delivery through an instant messaging application and email. The Gift Cards offer a
combination of discounts, convenience, flexibility, and controlled spending benefits: consumers can access price advantages
through upfront discounts, pre-allocate budgets for routine consumption to support disciplined spending, and brand-specific
promotions that may not be available through standard payment modes. This experience where a consumer can purchase a
brand-issued Gift Card on their smartphone and redeem it at the billing counter through prompt digital delivery, positions Gift
Cards as an alternative payment, particularly for price-sensitive consumers focused on affordability and value optimisation.

Our consumer-facing yayyy.shop website and mobile application both serve as a marketplace enabling the distribution of Gift
Cards and Prepaid Cards.

                                                                 218
Our Rewards and Loyalty business comprises: (i) reward points and our own reward points card, the “yayyy Reward Points
Card”, which can be purchased directly through our digital marketplace on the yayyy.shop website and mobile application and
used to redeem Gift Cards and Prepaid Cards available on our marketplace; and (ii) our RewardOn platform, a comprehensive,
end-to-end digital rewards and incentives platform that enables corporate customers to design, manage, and distribute reward
points to end-user beneficiaries, which can be redeemed digitally through a configurable rules engine integrated with a
customised catalogue of Gift Cards, Prepaid Cards and yayyy Reward Points Cards.




     2. Large and growing retail transacting user base with strong retention rates

We have built a large retail transacting user base, with transacting users increasing from 107,403 for the three months period
ended June 30, 2025 to 634,316 for the three months period ended June 30, 2026, and from 18,248 for Fiscal 2024 to 1,575,830
for Fiscal 2026, representing a CAGR of 829.28%. The large increase in the number of transacting users for Fiscal 2026 was
primarily attributable to launch of our digital marketplace, yayyy.shop, through which we began distributing Gift Cards in the
second quarter of Fiscal 2026, and the launch of our Rewards and Loyalty business in the second quarter of Fiscal 2026. During
Fiscal 2026 and the three months period ended June 30, 2026, we incurred user acquisition and retention expenses of ₹172.25
million and ₹97.64 million respectively, which primarily comprised user acquisition incentives paid to Ecosystem Partners for
referring new users to our platform. Accordingly, the increase in transacting users to 1,575,830 for the Fiscal 2026 and 634,316
for the three months period ended June 30, 2026, from 43,269 for the year ended March 31, 2025, was largely driven by our
user acquisition efforts through such Ecosystem Partners and launch of yayyy.shop and Rewards and Loyalty business in
second quarter of Fiscal 2026. This growth is underpinned by a strong user retention, with our User Retention Rate of 99.00%,
87.98% and 98.48% for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

Our Company has built and operates in-house, microservices-based technology platforms designed to handle high volumes of

transacting users in Fiscal 2026 and it allows for quick configuration and integration with third-party systems and our customers.
For further details on our technology, see “– Technology, Research and Development” on page 232.

save the time and effort of undertaking ground up development and lowering implementation risk. Furthermore, RewardOn is
our rewards and loyalty platform that supports the issuance, management, and redemption of reward points against a Prepaid
Card, yayyy Reward Points Card or a Gift Cards catalogue of 234 Gift Cards as at June 30, 2026, which is also offered on a

who want to launch a rewards and loyalty business.

Program managers are the most critical in the value chain (source: F&S Report, page 25). Issuers tie up with program managers
to scale user acquisition, engagement, and retention (source: F&S Report, page 20). Program managers orchestrate program
design, compliance operations, distribution, customer operations, and the spend-management software layer (source: F&S
Report, page 24). Program managers are primarily responsible for growing the volume and value of prepaid card transactions,
coordinating marketing, onboarding, and loyalty programs to expand the card’s user base (source: F&S Report, page 20). For
further details on program managers, see “Industry Overview – Prepaid cards & Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) spend
management market in India – 3.3 Direct to Consumer (D2C) Spend Management Market in India - Program manager as the
most critical stakeholder in the Value Chain” on page 168. There are significant barriers to entry to distribute Prepaid Cards,
as onboarding of distributors by PPI Partners typically involves rigorous empanelment and due diligence processes
encompassing compliance, technology, and operational assessments (source: F&S Report, page 25). This is a time-intensive
process, typically spanning 6–12 months, and only credible, established fintech players are able to successfully secure and
maintain such relationships (source: F&S Report, page 25). Developing or acquiring secure, scalable tech (fraud prevention,
encryption, uptime SLAs) capability is costly (source: F&S Report, page 25). Program managers must integrate with card
networks (Visa/Mastercard/RuPay) and payment gateways (source: F&S Report, page 26). Each network certification and
switch connection is time-consuming and complex (source: F&S Report, page 26). Attracting retail customers requires building
trust which new program managers struggle to achieve consumer confidence compared to established banks or fintech brands
(source: F&S Report, page 26).

Our ability to onboard and expand partnerships with PPI Partners and Gift Card Aggregators has supported the expansion of
our distribution network and the scaling of our offerings across our platforms.
